items.summary: Shell Egypt said it started production from Mina West field in the North East El Amriya concession in the Mediterranean Sea, supporting Egypt’s demand for gas. Dalia Elgabry, Vice President and Country Chair of Shell Egypt, said: “Bringing Mina West into production just three years after discovery demonstrates what we can achieve when we […]
items.excerpt: Shell Egypt said it started production from Mina West field in the North East El Amriya concession in the Mediterranean Sea, supporting Egypt’s demand for gas. Dalia Elgabry, Vice President and Country Chair of Shell Egypt, said: “Bringing Mina West into production just three years after discovery demonstrates what we can achieve when we […]
items.article_content:
Shell Egypt said it started production from Mina West field in the North East El Amriya concession in the Mediterranean Sea, supporting Egypt’s demand for gas.
Dalia Elgabry, Vice President and Country Chair of Shell Egypt, said: “Bringing Mina West into production just three years after discovery demonstrates what we can achieve when we work towards a shared goal from the outset.”
She added that together with the Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources, EGAS and KUFPEC, Shell Egypt aligned early on the decisions needed to move the project forward. This milestone is the result of that collaboration and the work of our teams and partners.
This adds a new source of domestic supply and strengthens the foundation for our continued investment in Egypt’s offshore gas resources, Elgabry added.
Operated by Mina West Gas Company, the field is connected through a new 7km pipeline to the existing West Delta Deep Marine infrastructure, which will transport gas to be processed at the Burullus gas facility before it enters Egypt’s domestic gas grid. Using existing infrastructure allowed the project to be delivered on an accelerated timeline.
The project is expected to produce 160 million standard cubic feet of gas per day (MMscf/d).

items.title: TeraMed launches Mediterranean renewable energy finance hub, targets $20bn by 2028
items.summary: The TeraMed Initiative has launched a Mediterranean Renewable Energy Finance Hub at COP31, aiming to accelerate clean-energy investment across the Arab and Mediterranean region and attract $20bn in investment commitments by 2028. The hub was unveiled during a high-level session on energy-transition finance attended by officials from Morocco, the United Nations, the European Commission and […]
items.excerpt: The TeraMed Initiative has launched a Mediterranean Renewable Energy Finance Hub at COP31, aiming to accelerate clean-energy investment across the Arab and Mediterranean region and attract $20bn in investment commitments by 2028. The hub was unveiled during a high-level session on energy-transition finance attended by officials from Morocco, the United Nations, the European Commission and […]
items.article_content:
The TeraMed Initiative has launched a Mediterranean Renewable Energy Finance Hub at COP31, aiming to accelerate clean-energy investment across the Arab and Mediterranean region and attract $20bn in investment commitments by 2028.
The hub was unveiled during a high-level session on energy-transition finance attended by officials from Morocco, the United Nations, the European Commission and the League of Arab States, alongside representatives of the Green Climate Fund and regional energy and financial institutions.
The initiative aims to strengthen coordination between governments, financial institutions and renewable-energy developers, improve project readiness, facilitate investment partnerships and address persistent barriers to financing. These include high capital costs, currency risks, fragmented regulatory frameworks and limited capacity for project preparation.
Moroccan Energy, Mines and Sustainable Development Minister Charafat Afailal said the two shores of the Mediterranean shared strong strategic complementarities and significant solar and wind resources.
She said TeraMed’s ambition to catalyse one terawatt of renewable-energy capacity by 2030 would require substantial investment and coordinated action by governments, financial institutions and the private sector.
Rania Al-Mashat, United Nations Under-Secretary-General and Executive Secretary of ESCWA, said investment in renewable energy needed to go hand in hand with electricity infrastructure, regional market integration and supportive policies.
She said TeraMed’s one-terawatt target provided a common direction for regional cooperation and highlighted opportunities to connect Mediterranean energy initiatives with the development of the Pan-Arab Electricity Market and interconnected power systems.
European Commissioner for the Mediterranean Dubravka Šuica welcomed the launch and its target of attracting $20bn in investment by 2028.
She said clean energy could serve as a bridge between the two shores of the Mediterranean, creating jobs, improving industrial competitiveness and strengthening regional economies.
Šuica added that the European Union’s Trans-Mediterranean Renewable Energy and Clean Tech Cooperation Initiative, known as T-MED, aims to mobilise an expected €25bn in investment by 2035 for renewable energy, electricity grids, interconnections and clean technologies.
Mahmoud Fathallah, Director of Environment at the League of Arab States’ General Secretariat, stressed the importance of stronger institutional cooperation across the region to advance the Arab energy-transition agenda and connect it with broader Mediterranean initiatives.
Hajar Khamlichi, North Africa Director at the Platform on International Energy, said the Mediterranean’s challenge was no longer simply recognising its renewable-energy potential but creating the conditions necessary to unlock investment on a large scale.
This would require aligning national policy priorities, project preparation and financial instruments, she said, adding that the real test of regional cooperation would be its ability to translate commitments into investment that accelerates renewable-energy deployment and strengthens regional economies.
Financing regional energy transition
TeraMed officials said the finance hub would provide technical assistance, strengthen policy coordination, develop regional pipelines of investment-ready projects and connect developers with potential financing partners.
They stressed that the hub was designed to complement, rather than duplicate, existing financing mechanisms by improving coordination among financial institutions, policymakers and project developers.
Francesco Corvaro, Special Envoy for Climate Change of the Italian government, participated in discussions on the role of climate diplomacy in supporting renewable-energy investment and regional cooperation.
Amgad Elmahdi, Head of the Middle East Region at the Green Climate Fund, contributed to discussions on improving project investment readiness and addressing barriers to accessing international climate finance.
Jauad El Kharraz, Senior Adviser at the TeraMed Initiative Coordination Unit, said the hub would focus on technical assistance, policy coordination, regional project pipeline development and matching projects with potential investors.
Iskander Erzini Vernoit, Co-founder and Executive Director of the IMAL Initiative for Climate and Development, highlighted the importance of complementing the existing financing architecture and addressing funding gaps facing small- and medium-scale renewable-energy projects.
Discussions also addressed the mobilisation of domestic capital, improvements to regulatory frameworks and stronger cross-border cooperation to accelerate renewable-energy deployment and industrial decarbonisation.
The finance hub forms part of TeraMed’s broader ambition to catalyse one terawatt of renewable-energy capacity across the Mediterranean by 2030.
The initiative said achieving this target would require investment not only in renewable-energy generation but also in electricity grids, cross-border interconnections, supportive regulatory frameworks and industrial electrification.
The next phase will focus on strengthening institutional partnerships, developing credible project pipelines and establishing financing pathways capable of translating the region’s renewable-energy potential into sustained investment, TeraMed said.

items.title: Petroleum minister represents Egypt at 20th Francophonie Summit in Cambodia
items.summary: Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Karim Badawi headed Egypt’s delegation, representing President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi, at the opening of the 20th Summit of Heads of State and Government of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF), held in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. The summit brought together leaders and government representatives from the organisation’s 90 member […]
items.excerpt: Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Karim Badawi headed Egypt’s delegation, representing President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi, at the opening of the 20th Summit of Heads of State and Government of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF), held in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. The summit brought together leaders and government representatives from the organisation’s 90 member […]
items.article_content:
Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Karim Badawi headed Egypt’s delegation, representing President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi, at the opening of the 20th Summit of Heads of State and Government of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF), held in Phnom Penh, Cambodia.
The summit brought together leaders and government representatives from the organisation’s 90 member countries.
The opening ceremony was attended by King Norodom Sihamoni of Cambodia, French President Emmanuel Macron, Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet and OIF Secretary-General Louise Mushikiwabo.
Held under the theme “Investing in Peace for Shared Prosperity and Lasting Stability”, the summit underscores the importance of strengthening cooperation and solidarity among member countries and intensifying joint efforts to promote peace, stability and sustainable development.
During the summit, Cambodia assumed the organisation’s rotating presidency from France for a two-year term, extending until the next summit in 2028.
Badawi is participating in the summit’s thematic plenary and closed sessions over its two days, presenting Egypt’s positions on the issues under discussion, efforts to promote peace and stability, and initiatives to support sustainable development.
He is also highlighting the importance of making greater use of cooperation mechanisms and joint initiatives within the OIF framework.
Badawi holds talks with international leaders
On the sidelines of the opening ceremony, Badawi held a series of meetings and informal discussions with heads of state and government and senior officials attending the summit. He was accompanied by Egypt’s Ambassador to Thailand and Cambodia, Hala Youssef.
The discussions focused on bilateral relations and opportunities to expand cooperation, particularly in the oil, gas and energy sectors.
During his meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron, Badawi conveyed President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi’s greetings and reaffirmed the strength of Egyptian-French relations, highlighting the longstanding partnership and close cooperation between the two countries across various fields.
The meeting also addressed the importance of maintaining coordination and consultations between Egypt and France, expanding bilateral cooperation and making use of the frameworks available through the OIF to promote dialogue and cooperation among member countries.
Badawi also met Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, Morocco’s Head of Government, to discuss the longstanding historical and fraternal ties between Egypt and Morocco.
The two sides explored ways to build on existing cooperation and strengthen partnerships across various sectors, particularly energy, oil and gas.
In a separate meeting, Badawi held talks with Xavier Bettel, Luxembourg’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs, Foreign Trade, Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Affairs. Discussions covered the strong relations between the two countries, opportunities to expand economic cooperation and prospects for collaboration in energy, oil and gas.
The minister also met OIF Secretary-General Louise Mushikiwabo to discuss cooperation between Egypt and the organisation, as well as Egypt’s active role in supporting joint initiatives that advance the OIF’s objectives and address the aspirations of its member countries.
Badawi also met Khaled El-Enany, Director-General of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO), on the sidelines of the summit.
Egypt participates in summit deliberations
Following the opening ceremony, Badawi, heading Egypt’s delegation on behalf of President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, participated in a session of the 20th OIF Summit alongside leaders and government representatives from member countries.
The session reviewed the outcomes of the organisation’s ministerial conference and discussed the Secretary-General’s report, as well as the main issues and topics on the summit’s agenda. Discussions focused on strengthening coordination and consultations among member countries on matters of common interest.
Egypt’s participation in the summit reflects its commitment to maintaining an active role within the OIF, strengthening relations with member countries and expanding cooperation in political, economic and investment fields to advance shared interests and create new partnership opportunities.
Further talks focus on African energy cooperation
On the sidelines of the summit, Badawi held additional bilateral meetings with senior officials, including Gabonese Foreign Minister Marie-Edith Tassyla.
The two sides discussed ways to advance bilateral relations and broaden cooperation, particularly in oil, natural gas and mining, while exploring opportunities to strengthen partnerships between the two countries in these sectors.
Badawi also met Morissanda Kouyaté, Guinea’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation, African Integration and Guineans Abroad.
Their discussions focused on strengthening cooperation between Egypt and Guinea and developing areas of joint engagement to serve their mutual interests.
The Petroleum Minister also held a further meeting with Xavier Bettel, Luxembourg’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs, Foreign Trade, Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Affairs.
The two sides discussed opportunities to develop economic and investment relations, exchanged views on issues of mutual interest and explored prospects for cooperation in energy, oil and natural gas.

items.title: Industry minister inspects five factories with combined investments of EGP 820m
items.summary: Industry Minister Khaled Hashem inspected five factories in the Third Settlement Industrial Zone, covering industrial robotics, vehicle interiors, electric vehicles, metering equipment and pharmaceuticals, as the government seeks to deepen local manufacturing, expand industrial automation and increase the domestic component in locally produced goods. The tour covered factories with combined investments of approximately EGP 820.2m, […]
items.excerpt: Industry Minister Khaled Hashem inspected five factories in the Third Settlement Industrial Zone, covering industrial robotics, vehicle interiors, electric vehicles, metering equipment and pharmaceuticals, as the government seeks to deepen local manufacturing, expand industrial automation and increase the domestic component in locally produced goods. The tour covered factories with combined investments of approximately EGP 820.2m, […]
items.article_content:
Industry Minister Khaled Hashem inspected five factories in the Third Settlement Industrial Zone, covering industrial robotics, vehicle interiors, electric vehicles, metering equipment and pharmaceuticals, as the government seeks to deepen local manufacturing, expand industrial automation and increase the domestic component in locally produced goods.
The tour covered factories with combined investments of approximately EGP 820.2m, according to figures provided by the companies, and highlighted their production capacities, export activities and plans to strengthen domestic industrial capabilities.
Hashem began his tour at Aria Technologies, a smart manufacturing solutions company specialising in industrial robots and automation systems. Established in 2020, the factory occupies 1,200 square metres and has investments of EGP 150m and capital of EGP 60m.
The facility has an annual production capacity of more than 100 industrial robots and smart vision systems, with a local component ratio of 40%. It records annual sales of EGP 250m and exports worth EGP 20m, while providing 85 direct and indirect jobs.
The company manufactures four types of linear industrial robots and offers smart vision systems, automated packaging and welding solutions, automated storage systems and industrial cloud applications. Its services also include industrial inspection, control and safety systems, energy consumption monitoring and predictive maintenance.
Hashem said industrial robotics and automation represent promising areas for strengthening the technological capabilities of Egypt’s industrial sector and supporting the transition towards smart manufacturing.
He urged companies operating in industrial technology to expand local manufacturing and increase the domestic component in their products to reduce reliance on imported systems.
The minister then visited Jeans Car Industry, which manufactures leather products and interior upholstery for vehicles, including aircraft, trains, cars and yachts.
The factory covers 1,500 square metres, with investments of EGP 46m and capital of EGP 7.5m. It produces approximately 25,000 seats annually, with a local component ratio of 50%, and employs 120 people.
The company has also established a free applied technology school in cooperation with the Ministry of Education and Technical Education to train technicians in vehicle interior manufacturing. Described by the company as the first of its kind in Egypt and the Middle East, the school currently has 250 students and graduated its first class last year.
Hashem said the ministry is prioritising the development of the automotive and vehicle components industries to reduce imports and strengthen Egyptian exports.
The tour also included Metgar Engineering and Trading, which specialises in sustainable transport solutions and electric vehicles. The factory occupies 25,000 square metres, with investments of EGP 72m and capital of EGP 500m.
Its products include electric golf carts, low-speed electric vehicles, electric scooters and beach buggies, with an annual production capacity of up to 12,000 units. The facility provides 380 direct and indirect jobs.
The company is also developing an electric vehicle as an alternative to tuk-tuks in cooperation with the Academy of Scientific Research, alongside a lithium battery project with VOL Tech.
Hashem also inspected Technometer Group, a manufacturer of meters and measurement and control equipment. The factory occupies 5,000 square metres, with investments of EGP 300m and capital of EGP 217m.
It has an annual production capacity of 720,000 meters, including water meters of different types and sizes, as well as measurement and control equipment for gases and liquids and copper castings. The factory’s local component ratio reaches 75%, while annual sales amount to EGP 1bn. It provides 312 direct and indirect jobs.
The company supplies products and services to the water, wastewater, irrigation, oil and gas sectors. Its production portfolio includes mechanical, prepaid and smart water meters, while its services cover calibration, leakage detection and water-loss reduction.
Hashem highlighted the factory’s 75% local component ratio, noting that domestic manufacturing of meters and measurement equipment plays an important role in modernising infrastructure and rationalising resource consumption.
He added that the ministry would continue supporting the industry and expanding export opportunities in regional and African markets.
The minister concluded his tour by inaugurating new production lines at Multi Care Egypt for Pharmaceutical Industries, following the completion of upgrades at the facility.
The factory occupies 5,200 square metres and has investments of EGP 252.2m and authorised capital of EGP 100m. It produces 12.2 tonnes annually of dietary supplements in powder and liquid forms and capsules, alongside approximately 30 million packs of human pharmaceutical products and specialised dietary supplements.
Its product range includes soft and hard capsules, creams, ointments, tablets, powders and fast-dissolving oral films. The factory has a local component ratio of 30%, annual sales of EGP 983.8m and exports worth EGP 38.6m. It provides 735 direct and indirect jobs.
The newly inaugurated production lines include facilities for soft gelatin capsules, creams and ointments, and fast-dissolving oral films, alongside upgraded warehouse facilities.
Hashem stressed that pharmaceutical manufacturing remains a priority in Egypt’s industrial strategy, particularly efforts to localise production and strengthen self-sufficiency. He said the new production lines would support the availability of medicines in the domestic market and help expand pharmaceutical exports.

items.article_content:
Egypt is experiencing stable autumn weather on Sunday, however, certain meteorological conditions warrant caution, most notably dense mists of which the Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) has issued a warning.
In some areas, this mist may intensify into a thick fog.
Cold Weather at Night
The EMA said that the weather on Sunday will be mild to moderately warm during the daylight hours across most regions, while remaining hot in parts of Upper Egypt.
As evening approaches, temperatures will drop, leading to cool to cold conditions in most areas—a trend that will persist into the early morning hours.
The most significant weather phenomenon is the dense water mist expected to form between two am and 10:00 am.
This will impact parts of the northern coast, Lower Egypt, Greater Cairo, the Suez Canal cities, central Sinai, and northern Upper Egypt.
In some locations, the mist may thicken into a dense fog, reducing horizontal visibility to less than 1,000 meters on certain roads.
Expected temperatures for Sunday:
Cairo and Lower Egypt: High 26C, low 17C.
Northern coasts (Alexandria and Matrouh): High 25C, low 16C.
Northern Upper Egypt: High 29C, low 13C.
Southern Upper Egypt: High 33C, low 15C.
Chances of Rain
Meteorological forecasts indicate a 40 percent probability of light to moderate, intermittent rain in the Halayeb and Shalateen regions.
There is also a very slight chance of light rain along the northwestern coasts.
Additionally, the EMA expects intermittent wind activity in parts of Greater Cairo and South Sinai, with speeds ranging between 30 and 35 km/h—a factor that may make the weather feel colder during the night hours.
Given the dangers posed by dense fog and reduced visibility, the EMA offered the following safety advice for drivers:
Maintaining a safe distance between vehicles.
Adhering to the designated speed limits and not exceeding them.
Avoiding the use of high-beam headlights, as they make it even harder to see in foggy conditions.
Keeping vehicle windows slightly open while driving to improve visibility.
Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm
The post Stable autumn weather, cold at night, and dense fog on Sunday appeared first on Egypt Independent.

items.article_content:
Hundreds of schools across Italy were evacuated on Wednesday after bomb threats were sent to about 6,300 institutions, becoming the latest in a series of incidents targeting infrastructure across Europe.
Schools in Scotland, Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland also received emails Wednesday, although police warned these were likely hoaxes and education facilities were not evacuated.
Italian police told CNN that hundreds of schools in the country were evacuated. Officials later said that the incident was a suspected hoax.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni later said in a video statement that all threats were deemed fake, with no concrete evidence of an attack, but didn’t rule out such threats resurfacing.
“It’s possible that messages such as these will arrive again. That is not the sign that something is not working, but rather the proof that those who send them have nothing left,” Meloni said, while urging against speculative finger-pointing as to who was behind the messages.
Authorities were investigating the source of the email, the police spokesperson said, declining to confirm the email address the communication came from.
About 6,300 schools across Italy received the e-mail threat, a spokesperson for the Italian public education ministry told CNN Wednesday. “It’s unclear how many have been evacuated, that is a decision taken locally under the advice of local authorities,” the spokesperson added.
Students and parents gather in a garden outside Bacone primary school after students were evacuated following a bomb threat across all school sites in Milan, Italy, on Wednesday.
Luca Bruno/AP
In central Rome, dozens of kindergarten and primary school children enjoyed a day off as the Quirinio Visconti primary school was evacuated. Their parents were notified to pick them up, a teacher told CNN.
The Italian prime minister said the government was “doing everything necessary to ensure the safety of citizens.”
Schools in UK and Ireland also receive emails
In Northern Ireland, more than 300 schools received a threatening email, police said Wednesday, adding that the message originated outside the United Kingdom and was being treated as a hoax.
“Our enquiries are ongoing, however, at this stage we consider risk to the public as low,” Assistant Chief Constable Anthony McNally said in a statement.
The Education Authority said the message sent to “a large number of schools” in Northern Ireland resembled a hoax sent to schools last month and that it was unaware of any evidence of a “credible” threat.
Police in the Republic of Ireland said a generic communication was sent to “a number of educational establishments” Wednesday. Police assessed the threat as “not credible” and said they were not advising any evacuations.
Dublin teacher Sharon Magee told CNN her school received a bomb threat at 10:55 a.m. local time (5:55 a.m. ET), but it was not evacuated.
“We were just told to keep alert in case we noticed anything on the premises and then the day just went ahead as normal,” she said, adding that everyone at the school got through the day safely.
Meanwhile, Police Scotland said “threatening messages” were sent to schools. The force said the messages were being treated as hoaxes and advised schools that the emails alone did not warrant evacuation.
Wave of disruption across Europe
Wednesday’s incident is the latest in a series targeting infrastructure and organizations across Europe.
“Everyone can be a target and that makes it harder to defend ourselves 100%,” Italian Defense Minister Guido Crosetto told CNN the day before hundreds of schools were evacuated Wednesday, describing efforts by Italian authorities to combat attacks.
“The goal of this hybrid warfare is to destroy this sovereignty and generate panic,” Crosetto said.
Last week, a string of hoax bomb threats disrupted dozens of flights and targeted media organizations across the continent.
And in the last few weeks, cyberattacks have hit supermarket refrigeration systems in France, Sweden, Belgium and Ireland.
The European Union said last week it was too early to tell whether the bomb threat incidents were linked, while security analysts and government ministers have suggested the wave could be part of a wider hybrid campaign or series of malicious hoaxes.
This story has been updated with developments.
CNN’s Niamh Kennedy and Farida Elsebai contributed reporting.

items.article_content:
New York — The Democratic Socialists of America’s New York City chapter officially urged Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez on Saturday to launch a presidential run in 2028.
The resolution passed by the New York City DSA is not an official endorsement. But it is the latest effort by democratic socialists to urge Ocasio-Cortez, one of the most prominent members of their movement, to run for the White House. Gustavo Gordillo, co-chair of the local DSA chapter, described the resolution as “a commitment to encouraging and building the foundation for a presidential campaign.”
“AOC and New York City DSA are committed to building a stronger democratic socialist movement and DSA will create the conditions for a presidential campaign capable of advancing a working-class political agenda,” Gordillo said during a press conference after the convention.
DSA chapters in Atlanta, Colorado, Los Angeles and Ithaca, New York, have already approved resolutions encouraging her to run. The resolutions also offer a glimpse of the priorities the chapters want Ocasio-Cortez to champion, including imposing an arms embargo on Israel, abolishing US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and enacting Medicare for All and the Green New Deal.
A spokesperson for Ocasio-Cortez, who rejoined the DSA in August after letting her membership lapse, did not return a request for comment.
The AOC resolution frames her potential presidential bid as a chance to champion working-class voters and expand DSA’s national influence.
The resolution passed 291-123. During debate prior to the vote, some members expressed opposition to the resolution over their belief that Ocasio-Cortez has strayed from DSA’s core identity and its priorities. They also expressed concern a resolution encouraging a run would confuse an endorsement process expected to follow.
DSA members have had previous disagreements about Ocasio-Cortez and her policies. In 2024, the national DSA withdrew its endorsement of her, saying she had failed to meet the group’s required criteria regarding the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
Gordillo downplayed any dissent, saying the organization rarely reaches unanimous votes on its resolutions. He warned that dissent is not correlated with grassroots organizing, and that organization members would be ready to become foot soldiers for a democratic socialist presidential campaign.
“When we allow dissent, when we allow people to pose constructive critiques of our elected officials, it makes them buy into the movement, Gordillo said. “We actually have a strong history of doing just that with the congresswoman, where we have not always been aligned on some of her positions on Palestine, and we’ve been able to work together and strengthen both DSA and her own platform. I think that’s what we’re committing to doing here.”
Ocasio-Cortez has said she would decide her next political move after the midterms. She is openly considering a White House or US Senate run and as she considers both options, she has said she is weighing her ethnicity, her personal life, her age and which path is more likely to deliver a win.

items.article_content:
A federal judge halted President Donald Trump’s plan to renovate a municipal golf course in Washington, DC, on Saturday night, issuing a temporary order that requires the administration keep the course open after Trump said it would be closed on Sunday for the overhaul.
US District Judge Ana C. Reyes said the administration’s push to revamp East Potomac Golf Links into the championship course Trump desires – one of several construction projects the president has sought as part of his effort to remake Washington to his tastes and leave a legacy – likely violated environmental law and ran afoul of procedural guardrails for executive branch actions.
She said the Justice Department’s arguments in the litigation, where it claimed that the November 15 closure was happening for safety reasons, were “pretextual.”
“The Government proposes to close a historic park, daily enjoyed by Washingtonians of all stripes, indefinitely,” Reyes wrote, finding that the closure would “irreparably harm” the plaintiffs in the case, individual golfers and preservationists.
In a statement following the ruling, the DOJ said it will “always vociferously defend the Trump Administration’s agenda in court.”
“The Court has acknowledged that the National Park Service can limit access to its facilities where the public is at risk of harm,” a DOJ spokesperson told CNN. “Nothing in the Court’s order precludes planning for the development of a world class golf course to continue.”
It’s the latest development in a monthslong battle between Reyes and the Trump administration – one that has prompted Trump smearing the judge on social media and suggestions from Reyes that government attorneys may have misled her.
The Justice Department has unsuccessfully tried to remove her from the case, brought by preservationists and golfers seeking to stop the redevelopment arguing that changing the course would run afoul of federal environmental regulations and diminish public access.
Trump, an avid golfer, first publicly proposed the idea of taking over and expanding the municipal golf course in May and was soon thereafter seen touring the grounds with Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and Tom Fazio, a well known golf designer who worked on several of Trump’s private courses.
The president initially said work on the East Potomac Links would begin September 1, which accelerated the legal challenge.
Saturday, the president continued to promote the project and posted photos of what he has called “Trash Island.”
“Unfortunately, Judge Ana Reyes doesn’t want us to quickly and inexpensively fix up the Course which is, also, very dangerous — The Fairways are far too close together,” Trump said in a social media post. “When you walk down the corridors of Trash Island, you don’t hear the sound of the running Potomac, all you hear is the sound of people screaming, ‘FORE!’”
In recent months, Reyes has expressed growing frustration with the administration.
In October, Reyes issued a stark order blocking tree removal and imposing new notice requirements after over 400 trees were removed from the course with minimal notice.
“More than just being upset and furious right now, I am just beyond disappointed with the government,” Reyes said during that hearing.
The administration claimed the removals were necessary and not tied to Trump’s desired renovation, a claim Reyes said she was “skeptical” of in last month’s hearing.
“The question goes to whether or not I have been lied to, whether I have been lied to in declarations about the plans, whether I have been lied to about the timing of things,” Reyes told Justice Department lawyers at the time.
The legal rationale of her ruling Saturday night turned on the National Park Service’s failures to take certain steps before overhaul that she found to be required by law – such has providing notice to the public of the plan and soliciting their comment on it.
“Notice-and-comment rulemaking is not impracticable merely because NPS wishes to accommodate President Trump and close the Park by November 15,” she wrote.
While the stakes surrounding the course have been comparatively low when put up against other legal battles roiling the Trump administration, the case has been one of several in which the administration has bristled at complying with court orders.
Other projects, such as the president’s efforts to rename the Kennedy Center, build a triumphal arch on the banks of the Potomac and construct a ballroom, are also all facing legal challenges.
This story was updated with additional information.
CNN’s Aleena Fayaz contributed to this report.

items.title: Egypt, Vietnam discuss cooperation in manufacturing, technology transfer
items.summary: Minister of State for Military Production Salah Gamblat received Nguyen Nam Duong, Ambassador of Vietnam to Cairo, and an accompanying delegation to discuss ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation and explore new partnership opportunities in manufacturing and technology. The meeting comes as part of Egypt’s efforts to expand international partnerships and strengthen industrial cooperation with friendly […]
items.excerpt: Minister of State for Military Production Salah Gamblat received Nguyen Nam Duong, Ambassador of Vietnam to Cairo, and an accompanying delegation to discuss ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation and explore new partnership opportunities in manufacturing and technology. The meeting comes as part of Egypt’s efforts to expand international partnerships and strengthen industrial cooperation with friendly […]
items.article_content:
Minister of State for Military Production Salah Gamblat received Nguyen Nam Duong, Ambassador of Vietnam to Cairo, and an accompanying delegation to discuss ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation and explore new partnership opportunities in manufacturing and technology.
The meeting comes as part of Egypt’s efforts to expand international partnerships and strengthen industrial cooperation with friendly countries.
The talks were held in line with President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi’s directives to enhance cooperation with the international private sector, attract foreign investment and localise modern technologies, supporting government efforts to develop domestic industry and increase reliance on locally manufactured products.
These efforts also seek to capitalise on Egypt’s strategic geographical location as a gateway to European, African and other global markets.
During the meeting, Gamblat reviewed the Ministry of Military Production’s advanced manufacturing capabilities, noting that it oversees 15 industrial companies and four service companies operating within an integrated system that combines defence and civilian industries.
He said the ministry benefits from advanced industrial and technological infrastructure, as well as extensive accumulated expertise.
Gamblat explained that military production companies have diverse defence manufacturing capabilities, including producing ammunition of various calibres and manufacturing and developing tanks, mortars and artillery.
Their capabilities also extend to radar systems, communications equipment and electronic warfare systems.
He added that surplus production capacity is directed towards serving the civilian sector, including maintenance and repair services provided by the Maintenance, Supplies and Integrated Solutions Company, as well as communications and information systems services offered by Touya Technology.
These activities, he said, reflect the diversity of the ministry’s industrial base and its ability to meet specialised manufacturing requirements.
Gamblat also highlighted the role of the Centre of Scientific and Technological Excellence, which brings together highly qualified professionals to link scientific research with industrial applications and turn research and development outcomes into commercially viable products.
He said the centre contributes to promoting innovation and supporting technology localisation.
The minister also reviewed the ministry’s capabilities in producing ferrous and non-ferrous castings, steel and other supporting industrial products that are essential to deepening local manufacturing.
Gamblat announced the ministry’s intention to participate in the Vietnam International Defence Expo 2026, describing the event as an important opportunity to showcase the industrial and technological capabilities of military production companies.
He said participation would also provide an opportunity to establish direct communication with international companies and institutions and explore prospects for partnerships and joint manufacturing.
For his part, the Vietnamese ambassador welcomed the meeting and the Ministry of Military Production’s invitation to participate in the exhibition.
He affirmed Vietnam’s interest in establishing joint industrial partnerships with the ministry’s companies across several sectors, drawing on the expertise and manufacturing capabilities of both countries to advance mutual interests and support technology transfer and exchange.
The Vietnamese side also expressed particular interest in cooperation in defence industries, information systems and technological transformation.
The ambassador highlighted the possibility of exploring cooperation in these areas through Touya Technology, an affiliated company of the Ministry of Military Production, to benefit from its expertise and capabilities in developing technological solutions and information systems.
At the conclusion of the meeting, both sides expressed their commitment to building on the discussions and translating the proposed areas of cooperation into concrete implementation measures and practical partnerships.
They said these efforts would strengthen economic and industrial relations between Egypt and Vietnam and create broader opportunities for cooperation between institutions and companies in both countries.

items.title: Holcim Egypt restarts fifth cement production line after EGP 1.3bn investment
items.summary: Egyptian Minister of Industry Khaled Hashem said the building materials sector, particularly cement manufacturing, is a key pillar of the national economy, given its role in supporting infrastructure, housing, urban expansion and major national projects. His remarks came during a ceremony marking the restart of the fifth production line at Holcim Egypt’s cement plant in […]
items.excerpt: Egyptian Minister of Industry Khaled Hashem said the building materials sector, particularly cement manufacturing, is a key pillar of the national economy, given its role in supporting infrastructure, housing, urban expansion and major national projects. His remarks came during a ceremony marking the restart of the fifth production line at Holcim Egypt’s cement plant in […]
items.article_content:
Egyptian Minister of Industry Khaled Hashem said the building materials sector, particularly cement manufacturing, is a key pillar of the national economy, given its role in supporting infrastructure, housing, urban expansion and major national projects.
His remarks came during a ceremony marking the restart of the fifth production line at Holcim Egypt’s cement plant in Ain Sokhna, following a seven-year shutdown, after investments exceeding EGP 1.3bn.
The minister’s speech was delivered on his behalf by Mohamed Zada, Assistant Minister of Industry for Strategic Industries, in the presence of representatives of the Swiss Embassy in Egypt, public- and private-sector partners, and Holcim’s global and local executives.
Attendees included Miljan Gutovic, CEO of Holcim Group; Khaled El-Dakany, Regional Head of Asia, Middle East and Africa at the group; and Medhat Ismail, CEO of Holcim Egypt.
Hashem said restarting the production line marks an important milestone for Holcim Egypt and reflects broader efforts across the country’s industrial sector to expand production capacity, reactivate industrial assets and maximise their utilisation.
The restarted line is expected to create 560 direct and indirect jobs, he added, noting that Egypt’s cement industry has a strong industrial base comprising 19 multinational companies, reflecting the country’s attractiveness as a destination for industrial investment.
Egypt ranks eighth globally and first in Africa among cement producers, he said, adding that its strategic geographical location, port network, logistics infrastructure, skilled workforce and access to regional and international markets provide competitive advantages for long-term industrial investment.
Hashem also highlighted the importance of Holcim’s presence in Egypt, noting that the group operates one of the world’s largest cement plants in the country, underscoring the Egyptian market’s significance within its global investment portfolio.
Addressing industrial competitiveness, Hashem said energy availability and costs are among the main factors determining production costs and the competitiveness of finished products in domestic and international markets.
He stressed that sustainable industrial growth requires not only expanding production capacity but also ensuring reliable energy supplies at competitive prices and improving energy efficiency.
Hashem added that the Ministry of Industry strongly encourages greater reliance on alternative fuels, particularly refuse-derived fuel (RDF), highlighting Holcim’s environmental and resource-efficiency efforts through its Geocycle platform, which focuses on the use of alternative fuels.
Egypt already has advanced industrial expertise in this field, Hashem said, expressing the ministry’s interest in attracting further investment in waste treatment, recycling and the conversion of waste into alternative energy sources.
He pointed out that these initiatives go beyond reducing reliance on conventional fuels, contributing to the development of a circular economy, more efficient resource utilisation and the achievement of environmental targets.
The minister also highlighted Egypt’s industrial capacity to serve regional and international markets, stressing the need for an integrated approach built around three priorities: maximising the utilisation of existing production capacity, increasing exports and foreign currency earnings, and ensuring sufficient supplies to meet domestic demand while avoiding unjustified price pressures.
“The ministry aims to establish a balanced industrial environment that ensures sustainable production and meets local market needs while enabling export growth and improving the competitiveness of Egyptian products in foreign markets,” he concluded.

items.title: Planning minister discusses start-up financing with leading US venture capital funds
items.summary: Planning and Economic Development Minister Ahmed Rostom held a series of meetings with senior executives from leading US venture capital funds and investment institutions at the conclusion of his participation in the B20 Summit 2026 in Washington, DC, to explore ways to attract foreign private sector investment into Egypt’s entrepreneurship and start-up sector. Rostom met […]
items.excerpt: Planning and Economic Development Minister Ahmed Rostom held a series of meetings with senior executives from leading US venture capital funds and investment institutions at the conclusion of his participation in the B20 Summit 2026 in Washington, DC, to explore ways to attract foreign private sector investment into Egypt’s entrepreneurship and start-up sector. Rostom met […]
items.article_content:
Planning and Economic Development Minister Ahmed Rostom held a series of meetings with senior executives from leading US venture capital funds and investment institutions at the conclusion of his participation in the B20 Summit 2026 in Washington, DC, to explore ways to attract foreign private sector investment into Egypt’s entrepreneurship and start-up sector.
Rostom met with Bobby Franklin, President and CEO of the US National Venture Capital Association (NVCA), and Brad Fierstein, Partner and Co-Head of Corporate Solutions for the Americas and Head of Deal Origination at Apollo Infrastructure Group.
During the meetings, Rostom outlined the main features of a comprehensive financing initiative that the Ministry of Planning and Economic Development plans to launch, including the establishment of a dedicated fund to support start-ups and entrepreneurs.
He explained that the initiative aims to broaden access to financing for promising Egyptian companies, strengthen their capacity to scale up their operations and attract more capital into the innovation ecosystem, in line with presidential directives and the recommendations of Egypt Forum 2026.
Rostom highlighted the ministry’s strategic vision of using financing as an effective tool to stimulate investment and matching companies’ financing needs with their respective stages of growth.
He noted that the proposed fund would play a key role in addressing funding gaps faced by start-ups as they progress from product development and business model testing to commercial expansion and entry into regional and international markets.
The minister also highlighted the link between the proposed financing initiative and the Qimam programme, which is designed to support high-growth start-ups with significant economic potential.
He stressed that financing alone is insufficient and must be complemented by investment-readiness support, management capacity development and the adoption of corporate governance standards to facilitate these companies’ access to international investor networks.
Rostom invited representatives of US funds and investment institutions to participate in investment funds targeting Egyptian start-ups.
He emphasised that the Egyptian market offers promising investment opportunities and innovative talent capable of generating added value, underscoring the importance of building sustainable international partnerships that translate innovation into tangible opportunities for inclusive economic growth.
As part of efforts to strengthen engagement with the international business community, Rostom also attended an official dinner hosted by the Advisory Council of the American Chamber of Commerce, bringing together representatives of major US companies and Egyptian entrepreneurs living abroad.
The gathering featured discussions on ways to deepen economic, trade and investment relations between Egypt and the United States, as well as measures to accelerate trade flows.
Rostom also outlined the main features of Egypt’s National Economic Transformation Programme and highlighted positive developments in the Egyptian economy, encouraging investors to explore opportunities to expand their operations in Egypt amid the reforms being implemented by the government.

items.title: Egypt and 17 countries condemn Israeli strike on Gaza’s Nasser hospital, urge US to enforce ceasefire
items.summary: Egypt and 17 other Arab and Muslim-majority countries have condemned “in the strongest terms” an Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, which their foreign ministers said caused casualties among patients and medical staff. In a joint statement, the ministers said the strike violated international humanitarian law, which gives special […]
items.excerpt: Egypt and 17 other Arab and Muslim-majority countries have condemned “in the strongest terms” an Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, which their foreign ministers said caused casualties among patients and medical staff. In a joint statement, the ministers said the strike violated international humanitarian law, which gives special […]
items.article_content:
Egypt and 17 other Arab and Muslim-majority countries have condemned “in the strongest terms” an Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, which their foreign ministers said caused casualties among patients and medical staff.
In a joint statement, the ministers said the strike violated international humanitarian law, which gives special protection to medical facilities and health workers. They also condemned continued Israeli attacks on civilians, including strikes on tents and other sites sheltering displaced people, saying these undermined the ceasefire and were inconsistent with US President Donald Trump’s Comprehensive Plan for Gaza.
Alongside Egypt, the statement was signed by the foreign ministers of Qatar, Sudan, Libya, Palestine, Djibouti, Somalia, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Mauritania, Jordan, the UAE, Türkiye, Pakistan, Algeria, Lebanon, Indonesia and Kuwait. It did not give a casualty figure.
Winter warning
The ministers expressed grave concern that Israeli restrictions on humanitarian aid, shelter materials including tents, caravans and mobile homes, and medical supplies were deepening Gaza’s humanitarian catastrophe as winter approaches. Inadequate shelter and failing water, sanitation and health services put civilians at grave risk, they said, particularly children and infants, “who could once again die from exposure to freezing temperatures”.
They called on Israel to heed appeals from the international community and the Board of Peace for more aid, and to meet in full its obligations under the Sharm El-Sheikh Agreement, the Trump plan and UN Security Council Resolution 2803 of 2025. That includes upholding the ceasefire, protecting civilians and medical facilities, allowing aid, shelter and early-recovery equipment in sufficient quantities, and letting UN agencies and humanitarian groups work without obstruction.
No conditions on aid
The ministers said these first-phase commitments were due to take effect on signature and that Israel must implement them without further delay or additional conditions, including political and security conditions that impede humanitarian access. Urgent humanitarian assistance must proceed independently of progress on later phases of the plan, they said.
They called on the United States and the Board of Peace, “within their respective roles”, to step up efforts to ensure Israel fully implements its commitments and lifts all restrictions on aid, “thereby preserving the credibility of the agreements and consolidating the ceasefire”.

items.article_content:
Egypt’s Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty met his Russian, Ukrainian and Polish counterparts on the sidelines of the Sir Bani Yas Forum in the United Arab Emirates, using the talks to press for a negotiated end to the war in Ukraine and to protect the grain supplies on which Egypt depends.
Abdelatty met Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha on Friday 13 November, and Russia’s Sergei Lavrov and Poland’s Radosław Sikorski on Saturday 14 November, according to statements from foreign ministry spokesman Ambassador Nader Zaki. He also met Serbia’s Foreign Minister Marko Đurić.
Talks with Lavrov
With Lavrov, Abdelatty praised the strategic partnership between Egypt and Russia and pointed to the meeting between President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the third Russia-Africa summit in October.
The two discussed the effect of regional tensions on maritime security, international trade and food security. Abdelatty stressed the need for greater international efforts to secure shipping lanes and keep strategic goods flowing.
Ukraine and the Black Sea
In his meeting with Sybiha, Abdelatty said Egypt supported a peaceful settlement through dialogue and diplomacy that would end the conflict and its consequences, guarantee freedom of navigation in the Black Sea and keep grain supply chains stable. The two ministers said they wanted to expand ties in trade, food security and energy.
Abdelatty also told Sybiha that Egypt was keen to host a global centre for storing, supplying and trading grain, pointing to its geography, infrastructure and logistics.
He repeated Egypt’s call for a peaceful settlement in Ukraine and for freedom of navigation in the Black Sea when he met Sikorski.
Talks with Sikorski
Meeting Poland’s Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski, Abdelatty expressed pride in the historic relations between Egypt and Poland, which will mark their centenary in 2027. The two ministers also discussed the war in Ukraine, with Abdelatty reiterating Egypt’s support for a peaceful settlement through dialogue and diplomacy that would end the conflict and its humanitarian and economic consequences, guarantee freedom of navigation in the Black Sea and keep grain supply chains stable.

items.article_content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly began a field visit to Dakahleya on Saturday to inspect several service and development projects, including factories operating in the Mit Ghamr Investment Zone, as the government seeks to address obstacles facing ongoing projects, accelerate their operations and encourage further industrial investment.
The visit also includes inspections of food exhibitions, housing projects under the national project to develop governorate capitals, the plasma donation centre in Mansoura and the new liver transplant centre at Mansoura University.
Madbouly said the tour aims to follow up on development projects across several sectors and assess challenges requiring coordination among ministries and state agencies to resolve.
He added that the food exhibitions are intended to ensure the availability of a range of essential commodities to citizens at affordable prices, while visits to industrial facilities reflect the government’s commitment to supporting manufacturing, attracting investment and creating jobs.
The prime minister was accompanied by Higher Education and Scientific Research Minister Abdelaziz Konsowa, who is also acting Minister of Culture; Investment and Foreign Trade Minister Mohamed Farid Saleh; Industry Minister Khaled Hashem; Dakahleya Governor Tarek Marzouk; Urban Development Fund Chairman Khaled Seddik; and General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) CEO Mohamed Awad, alongside members of parliament and local executive officials.
Mit Ghamr zone reaches full occupancy
Madbouly began his visit by inspecting the Mit Ghamr Investment Zone, affiliated with GAFI, which covers 18 feddans. The zone has reached full occupancy, with 107 industrial units of different sizes, attracting investments exceeding EGP 500m and generating around 2,500 job opportunities. A further 160 projects are on the waiting list, according to a presentation delivered during the visit.
The zone began operations in July 2021 and offers industrial units measuring 144, 288 and 576 square metres, providing flexible spaces for businesses operating in engineering, electronics and metal industries.
Madbouly described investment zones as a successful model for supporting small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and providing sustainable employment opportunities for young people in governorates. He said the government is continuing to improve the investment climate and provide support for deepening local manufacturing and strengthening the competitiveness of Egyptian products in domestic and international markets.
He called for expanding the investment-zone model to new cities and other governorates, highlighting its potential to attract investment and support industrial activity beyond major urban centres.
Farid said investment zones are an important tool for localising economic development and deepening domestic manufacturing through the establishment of integrated industrial clusters across governorates. He added that developing these zones and making better use of their production capabilities would help attract investment and create an environment conducive to production and business expansion.
Dakahleya Governor Tarek Marzouk said the diversity of industrial activities in the Mit Ghamr zone reflects the governorate’s production capabilities, skilled workforce and industrial expertise, particularly in Mit Ghamr, which has a long history of manufacturing and craftsmanship.
Broad range of locally manufactured products
During the visit, Madbouly toured an exhibition showcasing products made by companies operating in the zone, reviewing their manufacturing activities, production processes, reliance on locally sourced components and raw materials, and potential to expand exports.
The exhibits included aluminium cookware, pharmacy supplies and hardware, valves and water mixers, LED bulbs and lighting fixtures, refrigerator coils, personal care products such as shower gels, shampoos and oils, fans, ventilation equipment, mosquito zappers and dental supplies.
Other products included office furniture and school desks, laboratory and diagnostic reagents, metal cabinets and other metal products, central air-conditioning equipment, cooling and ventilation units, and metal, plastic and paper packaging. The exhibition also featured engineering and electrical products, including cooker timers, touch-sensitive electrical switches and devices designed to protect against electrical current fluctuations.
Participating companies included Taiba Al-Ayadi, Yebito Supplies, Miawy Metal Forming, Al Amer Group, Dawood Refrigeration Products, Al Andalus Perfumes and Cosmetics, Egyptian Electrical and Home Appliances Manufacturing and Assembly, Avanti Medical, Scopas, Siamco for Contracting and Metal Forming, Zain Egypt for Engineering Industries and Works, Alpha Omega, Egyptian Tinplate and Plastics, and Eco Star Engineering Industries, among others.
Madbouly stressed the importance of enabling local manufacturers to serve the domestic market while continuing to expand exports, noting that greater reliance on locally manufactured products could reduce imports and ease demand for foreign currency.
One cosmetics manufacturer told the prime minister that its factory uses 100% Egyptian raw materials and initially directed all its production towards export markets. The company is preparing to launch its products in the domestic market in the coming period.
Madbouly also visited the pavilion of BIG EDUCATION, which was established in 2018 as a brand of BIG Investment and Development Group.
The business initially operated with five employees and investments of EGP 250,000, focusing on designing school furniture and outsourcing its production. It later established a presence in the Mit Ghamr zone and received its first factory in 2025.
The prime minister said Egyptian factories should make greater use of their production capacity to meet local demand while maintaining their presence in export markets. He also highlighted the role of local manufacturing in replacing imported goods and strengthening the competitiveness of national industry.
ELC plans new factory in Sadat City
Madbouly also inspected ELC’s television manufacturing and assembly plant in the investment zone. The company produces conventional and smart television sets and has an annual production capacity of 100,000 units.
Company Chairperson Mohamed Mostafa El-Helwany said ELC was established in 2021 and began production in Mit Ghamr in 2022. The factory occupies 1,440 square metres, with investments of EGP 100m, and provides around 75 jobs.
The company distributes its television products across Egyptian governorates and exports part of its output to African and other international markets.
ELC plans to expand its manufacturing operations by establishing a new factory in Sadat City on a 7,000-square-metre site. The facility will produce interactive screens and television components, with production scheduled to begin in November 2027.
Madbouly noted that the electronics industry is among the sectors receiving government attention as part of efforts to strengthen Egypt’s industrial base and diversify production. He stressed the importance of expanding the local manufacture of technology products and leveraging the expertise and capabilities of Egyptian companies to meet a larger share of domestic demand.
The prime minister affirmed the government’s readiness to support ELC’s expansion plans to increase production and exports.
Arab Copper Centre produces 500,000 units annually
Madbouly also visited the Arab Copper Centre for Engineering Industries, which manufactures and assembles lighting fixtures and electrical panels.
Chairman Islam El-Nahas said the company was established in 2021 in the Mit Ghamr zone, occupying a 1,728-square-metre site with investments of approximately EGP 100m.

items.excerpt: Gold prices in Egypt’s domestic market recorded a sharp decline over the week from 7 to 14 November, with 21-karat gold, the most widely traded grade, falling from EGP 6,210 per gram last Saturday to EGP 5,950 on Saturday, according to data from iSagha, an online gold and jewellery trading platform. items.article_content:
Gold prices in Egypt’s domestic market recorded a sharp decline over the week from 7 to 14 November, with 21-karat gold, the most widely traded grade, falling from EGP 6,210 per gram last Saturday to EGP 5,950 on Saturday, according to data from iSagha, an online gold and jewellery trading platform.
According to the platform, the domestic decline reflected a global downturn following the release of US inflation figures for October, which came in above market expectations. The data strengthened expectations that the US Federal Reserve would maintain its restrictive monetary policy and potentially raise interest rates, while the dollar remained strong globally.
The platform noted that the dollar’s depreciation against the Egyptian pound added further downward pressure on gold prices in local currency, as the pound’s appreciation reduced the precious metal’s theoretical value.
Meanwhile, the widening gap between domestic gold prices and their theoretical value, calculated based on international ounce prices and the exchange rate, became increasingly apparent. The gap reached EGP 134.74 per gram, equivalent to 2.31%, on 12 November, highlighting the continued divergence between locally traded prices and levels justified by global market movements and exchange rates.
Saeed Embaby, Executive Director of iSagha, said the current pricing gap was neither normal nor healthy for the market, expressing concern that it had exceeded EGP 134 per gram.
He explained that the discrepancy meant consumers were not fully benefiting from falling international gold prices and the improvement in the exchange rate, but were instead continuing to pay more than the metal’s theoretical value.
Embaby said the decline in 21-karat gold from EGP 6,210 to EGP 5,950 per gram did not automatically mean that prices had become fair or that it was an appropriate time to buy.
He stressed that the more important question was not simply how much domestic prices had fallen, but how far they remained from their theoretical value.
Embaby added that a pricing gap of this magnitude required consumers to exercise caution and avoid rushing to buy in response to apparent price declines.
He warned that the gap was damaging the market even before affecting consumers, as it undermined confidence in pricing mechanisms, increased uncertainty and made it difficult for buyers to determine a fair purchase price.
He noted that a persistent gap could lead consumers to postpone purchasing decisions, weigh on trading activity and create the impression that the domestic market was not fully responding to international developments.
The iSagha executive explained that part of the pricing gap was linked to hedging by bullion traders, who feared a sudden rebound in international gold prices or the dollar exchange rate and sought to protect their financial positions by maintaining an additional margin.
However, he stressed that such hedging should not become a permanent burden on consumers or force buyers to bear the cost of future risks that had not yet materialised.
He said traders had the right to manage their risks, but consumers were equally entitled to transparent and fair prices that reflected movements in international gold prices and exchange rates.
Embaby argued that it was unreasonable for both international gold prices and the dollar to decline while domestic prices continued to carry a substantial premium justified by hedging.
He warned that allowing this situation to persist would undermine market balance and weaken trust between market participants.
Embaby urged consumers not to regard a price decline alone as a guaranteed buying opportunity.
He advised buyers to ask about gold’s theoretical value per gram, compare prices from several sellers, and enquire about making charges, hallmarking fees and any additional costs before completing a purchase.
He added that when the pricing gap was substantially negative, consumers would be better advised not to commit all their available funds to a single purchase, but instead to buy in stages and only if they had a genuine need for gold.
Embaby also advised consumers against buying out of fear that prices might rise again or accepting a price whose components they could not clearly understand.
He stressed that transparency was the solution and that narrowing the pricing gap was a shared responsibility among traders, trading platforms and the relevant authorities.
A strong market, he said, was one that protected consumers while allowing traders to manage their risks fairly.
Embaby concluded that consumers should not ask only how much gold prices had fallen, but also whether domestic prices had declined in proportion to movements in international gold prices and the dollar, and whether the pricing gap worked in their favour or against them.
He emphasised that not every price decline represented a buying opportunity and that not every quoted price was necessarily fair.

items.article_content:
The Israeli business newspaper Calcalist reported on Friday that the Emirati airline flydubai has extended the cancellation of its flights between Dubai and Ben Gurion Airport until December 15, amid the continued suspension of direct air travel between both nations.
The newspaper noted that Israeli airlines have yet to receive approval from security authorities to resume flights on this route – therefore direct air travel between Israel and Dubai will remain suspended for approximately another month and a half.
Flydubai suspended its flights to Israel on September 30, following an attempted hijacking of one of its aircraft during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv—an incident that resulted in an emergency landing at Tabuk Airport in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
The newspaper added that the airline subsequently announced the suspension of its operations to Israel, pending the completion of examinations and investigations into the incident.

items.article_content:
US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced on Friday the grounding of all departing flights from American airports due to a communications issue affecting air traffic control centers across the country.
Duffy said Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) technicians are investigating the communications problem, affirming that authorities will provide immediate updates as soon as more information becomes available.
CNN quoted the FAA as saying that the decision to ground departing flights resulted from communications issues impacting several air traffic control centers.
Is the cause a cyberattack?
Initial reports indicate that this is not a cyberattack, according to two law enforcement officials cited by CNN.
The last time the United States experienced a complete ground stop of flights was in January 2023, when a pilot notification system suffered an outage. Prior to that, the last nationwide ground stop was issued following the September 11, 2001 attacks, according to the American network.
Earlier, the FAA had issued an extremely “rare order” halting air traffic nationwide across all airports due to “exceptional circumstances” and “safety reasons,” according to Axios.
The air traffic control statement read: “All departing aircraft must remain grounded until further notice,” adding that “incoming international flights will be handled on a case-by-case basis.”
7,000 flights canceled
According to the flight-tracking website FlightAware, nearly 7,000 flights in the US have been delayed or canceled as a result of the FAA’s decision to suspend flights nationwide.
Technical glitch or terrorist act
For her part, an aviation expert suggested that the FAA’s decision to ground all departing flights in the United States was likely caused by a technical glitch rather than a terrorist act.
In remarks to CNN, aviation expert Mary Schiavo noted that the FAA had announced earlier today that it was preparing to activate a new artificial intelligence-based tool called SMART (Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Traffic) to help manage air traffic across the entire US airspace.
Schiavo explained that new computer systems sometimes face difficulties interfacing with legacy systems, pointing out that incompatibility between the systems could be behind the issue that led to the ground stop.
She added that one of the objectives of the SMART system is to manage air traffic mid-flight, providing a great deal of facilitation and flexibility.
She stressed that no information has emerged so far indicating that the FAA’s decision resulted from threats or a terrorist act, suggesting the cause is likely newer computer systems attempting to interact with older ones.
Meanwhile, The New York Times reported that notices related to the air traffic control system disappeared from an FAA website.
The air traffic tracking site Flightradar noted that approximately 3,100 aircraft are currently en route to US airports amid the ground stop on departures, adding that no flights have taken off from those airports.
The post All US flights grounded amid cyberattack speculation: What we know so far appeared first on Egypt Independent.

items.article_content:
Egypt has broken new ground in international digital trade, becoming the first country outside Europe to achieve full technical alignment with the European Union’s electronic signature and seal framework.
The milestone was cemented through a new administrative arrangement signed between Egypt’s Information Technology Industry Development Agency (ITIDA) and the European Commission.
By placing Egypt onto the EU’s Advanced Electronic Signatures (AdES) Trust List, the deal eliminates traditional cross-border paperwork bottlenecks, allowing Egyptian and European companies and government bodies to verify digital contracts, stamps, and official documents seamlessly across borders.
Why Egypt’s edge matters
A historic first: Out of every non-European nation worldwide, Egypt is the very first to pass the EU’s rigorous technical evaluation for electronic trust interoperability—positioning Cairo as a premier digital bridge between Europe, the Middle East, and Africa.
Regulatory leadership via ITIDA: Acting as Egypt’s root digital trust authority, ITIDA licenses, regulates, and audits local e-signature providers to meet strict international cybersecurity and encryption standards.
Two-way digital highway: Under the agreement, the European Commission will integrate Egypt’s trusted providers into its official third-country list, while ITIDA will mirror the EU’s trusted list inside Egypt—cutting red tape, accelerating deal closures, and boosting e-commerce competitiveness for Egyptian exporters and tech firms.
Fulfilling a flagship digital pledge from the October 2025 EU-Egypt Summit in Brussels, the pact turns Egypt’s domestic digital infrastructure into an internationally recognized engine for cross-border trade and investment.

items.article_content:
Egypt’s Ministry of Finance is turning prime state-owned land along the Red Sea coast into a high-value engine for debt reduction, unveiling a strategy centered on private-sector partnerships and major investment deals rather than straightforward land sales.
Under a new master plan for the Red Sea region, the government aims to unlock steady revenue streams by offering land under usufruct (long-term lease) agreements, launching joint ventures with private developers, and executing debt-for-investment swaps.
Proceeds from these deals will go directly toward paying down public debt and easing debt-service costs, while simultaneously freeing up budget space for social protection, healthcare, and education.
The push builds on Cairo’s broader fiscal tightening campaign, which has already trimmed the nation’s debt-to-GDP ratio from 96 percent to 81.9 percent over the past three years, alongside a primary budget surplus that hit 4.9 percent of GDP in the 2025/2026 fiscal year. Officials say landing blockbuster investment deals along the coast will be key to accelerating that downward debt trajectory.

Travelers passing through Cairo International Airport can now turn their pre-flight wait into a trip through time, following the launch of new, complimentary interactive photo kiosks across the terminals.
Equipped with artificial intelligence, the booths allow passengers to snap souvenir portraits and customize their backdrop by selecting from different historical eras. Users can instantly save the digital keepsakes or share them directly to social media—a move designed to add a playful, modern touch to the travel routine.
The rollout reflects a broader push by the Cairo Airport Company to rethink the passenger journey. Rather than focusing solely on check-in speed and transit logistics, airport operators are increasingly investing in digital entertainment and hospitality-driven amenities to match evolving global aviation standards.
The passenger-experience upgrades arrive amid sustained growth in air traffic at Egypt’s busiest aviation hub. In October 2026 alone, Cairo International Airport handled 2,781,163 passengers across 19,927 flights, underscoring steady operational momentum as the facility continues modernizing its infrastructure and services.

items.article_content:
Fueled by warm autumn weather and strong demand for Red Sea resorts, Egypt has claimed the top spot as the most sought-after international destination for Russian travelers this November, outpacing major rivals Turkey and Thailand.
According to data reported by the Russian state news agency RIA Novosti, Russian vacationers are willing to pay a premium for Egyptian getaways compared to competing markets.
The average trip to Egypt currently stands at approximately 274,000 rubles, edging out Thailand at 271,000 rubles and sitting well above Turkey’s average package cost of 221,000 rubles.
Industry observers attribute Egypt’s lead to its mild November climate, which offers an ideal escape as temperatures drop across Russia.
Coastal hubs along the Red Sea and South Sinai remain primary draws, bolstered by diverse itineraries that allow travelers to pair beach relaxation with cultural sightseeing—solidifying Egypt’s standing as a premier autumn destination for the Russian market.

Egypt’s national football team faces a crucial test against Malawi in Matchday 3 of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers.
Cairo International Stadium will host the match at 9:00 PM on Friday, marking the Pharaohs’ second home appearance of the qualifying campaign following their previous clash against Angola at the same venue.
Live broadcast coverage of the Egypt vs. Malawi qualifier will air exclusively on the beIN Sports network via beIN Sports 2 HD.
The fixture carries significant weight, as it marks the national team’s first match under newly appointed head coach Ali Maher, who recently took over from Hossam Hassan.

Goalkeeper: Mostafa Shobeir
Defenders: Ahmed Fatouh, Rami Rabia, Hossam Abdelmaguid, Mohamed Hany
