items.article_content:
On Friday, the Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) released its weather forecast and rainfall map, announcing a slight rise in temperatures across most regions.
Mild to warm autumn weather will prevail during the day across most areas, turning hot in southern Upper Egypt, while becoming cool to cold at night and during the early morning hours across most parts of the country.
Temperatures in Cairo are forecast to reach a high of 26°C with an overnight low of 16°C.
There are chances of light to occasionally moderate rain (approximately a 30 percent probability) at intermittent intervals over parts of Halayeb and Shalateen, alongside weak chances of light rain (around a 20 percent probability) over parts of the Northern Coast and northern Lower Egypt (Delta).
Low-lying clouds will also form over scattered areas of southern Lower Egypt, Greater Cairo, and the Suez Canal cities.
Satellite imagery detected intermittent wind activity reaching speeds of 30 to 35 km/h across most regions.

items.article_content:
Turkish Airlines launched scheduled flights between Istanbul and Chengdu on 11 November, making the western Chinese city its fourth destination in mainland China after Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou.
The airline will operate three flights a week to Chengdu Tianfu International Airport using Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner aircraft. Flight TK226 leaves Istanbul Airport on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays at 02:05, arriving in Chengdu at 15:40 local time. The return flight, TK227, departs Chengdu on Mondays, Thursdays and Saturdays at 00:45, landing in Istanbul at 05:55.
To mark the launch, the airline is offering fares from $540 between Istanbul and Chengdu.
A western China hub
Chengdu, home to more than 21mn people, is a centre for trade, logistics and finance, and hosts multinational companies in electronics, carmaking, aviation, biotechnology and artificial intelligence. Recognised by UNESCO as a City of Gastronomy, it draws millions of visitors a year with its Sichuan cuisine and its giant panda breeding and research base.
Murat Şeker, chairman of the board and executive committee of Turkish Airlines, said China held a strategically important position among the airline’s key markets. “We believe this new route will contribute to the continued growth of commercial, cultural and tourism ties between Türkiye and China,” he said.
Turkish Airlines, a member of the Star Alliance, operates a fleet of 571 passenger and cargo aircraft serving 359 destinations in 133 countries, according to the company.

The mad dash included a November 4 call from Republican Sen. items.article_content:
The Democrats’ coming takeover of the Senate has kickstarted a scramble to confirm two dozen of President Donald Trump’s judicial nominees before Republicans turn over the gavel in January.
The mad dash included a November 4 call from Republican Sen. Ted Cruz to a top lawyer in Trump’s Justice Department to solicit the lawyer’s interest in filing a seat in Texas, after the state elected James Talarico, a Democrat who will have veto power over district court nominees. Trump formally announced the nomination of T. Elliot Gaiser, the head of the DOJ’s Office of Legal Counsel, less than a week later.
But the compressed timeline has also heightened clashes between the White House and Republican senators over the president’s choices.
The stalemates already forced a switcheroo this week of Trump’s choice for an appeals court seat, potentially slowing down the timeline for filling it, while at least one other district court nomination in Oklahoma may be imperiled because of the resistance of a Republican home state senator.
Trump’s remaking of the judiciary – from the Supreme Court on down in his first term – could arguably be the longest-lasting legacy of his presidency. Right-leaning judges could continue to serve as a check on Democrats, by striking down their policies, if they expand their power in Washington in 2028 and beyond.
In his second term, Trump has not been able to match the record-breaking number of judicial confirmations he achieved in his first administration, particularly on influential appeals courts, as he returned to the White House with far fewer vacancies to fill than the start of his first term. Now, Republicans are anticipating the possibility that Democrats won’t allow any of his nominees to be confirmed once they take Senate control, raising the stakes for getting every possible judge approved in the next month and a half.
With little time to spend for negotiation over who the president selects, tensions are flaring within the conservative legal community over how local politics are getting in the way of confirming judges with the bona fides they prefer.
“Trump has set precedents where he will roll over for the state senators,” said Joshua Blackman, a South Texas College of Law professor and a conservative who has written extensively about judicial nomination battles. “And we have the picks who probably are not the best picks as a result.”
Republican leaders are juggling this infighting with the threats of Democratic procedural maneuvers that will jam up the process of confirming Trump’s nominees.
The Senate Judiciary Committee has set an aggressive calendar to push the remaining nominees through the pipeline – prompting Democratic accusations that the GOP is breaking Senate norms – while leadership is charting out a path for moving the nominees along on the Senate floor along with other priorities.
“We’re going to make every second count, and that means all these judicial appointments,” Wyoming Sen. John Barrasso, the Republican whip, said Tuesday. “We’re going to do everything we can to get every single one of them confirmed.”
GOP infighting over Trump’s choices
The first post-election Judiciary Committee meeting Tuesday kicked off with sparring between its chair, Iowa GOP Sen. Chuck Grassley and Sen. Dick Durbin, its top Democrat, about the lengths Republicans were willing to go to speed Trump’s nominees through.
But soon after, it became clear that the calendar was not the only problem.
Plans to for the committee to vote Tuesday on two nominees to Oklahoma’s federal court were derailed by the opposition that one of the nominees, Zachary West, faces from the junior senator from the state, Republican Sen. Alan Armstrong, according to a source familiar with the nominations process.
Supporting Armstrong in his opposition, according to the source, is North Carolina Sen. Thom Tillis, meaning that West would struggle to get out of the committee, which Tillis serves on.
So far, the White House is standing by Trump’s choice, with an official telling CNN Wednesday that the “President has selected two highly qualified nominees for the district court in Oklahoma, and we are confident they will be confirmed.”
But the White House on Tuesday night had to reverse course on a nomination for an Arkansas seat on the 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals, after the home state senators balked at the choice over their preferred candidate.
The canned nominee, US District Judge Lee Rudofsky, was widely celebrated by the conservative legal movement for the decisions he has issued from his current perch on the trial-level federal court in Arkansas. Rudofsky had already had his hearing and would have been primed for a vote out of the Judiciary Committee by next week.
The 8th Circuit already has a deep right-lean, but the seat had significance for Trump-aligned legal advocates because filling it will mean that he appointed a majority of judges on that court.
Now, Republicans will go back to square one and schedule a new hearing from the freshly announced nominee, Arkansas Supreme Court Justice J. Cody Hiland.
“The committee is carefully vetting Hiland’s nomination,” a committee spokesperson told CNN. “As chairman, Senator Grassley has discretion to set the committee’s schedule and is working to efficiently process President Trump’s pending judicial nominees.”
That conservative legal world was already grousing about the current nominee for a Mississippi seat on the 5th Circuit Trump is trying to fill this Congress, who has the support of the senior Republican senator from the state, Sen. Roger Wicker, but is not seen as a reliable vote for the right’s most cherished causes.
According to Blackman, the movement would have preferred a candidate like Mississippi Solicitor General Scott Stewart, who argued successfully at the Supreme Court for overturning nationwide abortion protections. The current nominee, Todd Butler, is a former clerk for the retiring 5th Circuit judge he is set to replace, and according to his application paperwork, he received outreach from Wicker before the vacancy was publicly announced.
“They’re jamming (the White House) up, and I think Trump is just going along with it because he has other stuff he’s worrying about,” Blackman said.
Like Texas, Mississippi flipped a Senate seat, with Democrat Scott Colom projected to beat Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith. (Colom, a local district attorney, ran for the seat after Hyde-Smith blocked his nomination to a judgeship by President Joe Biden).
When Trump announced Gaiser’s nomination on Tuesday, he also rolled out nominations for another judicial vacancy in Texas – choosing a Texas Supreme Court justice who just lost his reelection for that seat – and in South Carolina, which elected Democrat Annie Andrews to the Senate.
Democrats have speculated that local politics could get in the way of confirmation of Gaiser, and Texas Sen. John Cornyn, a retiring Republican who also sits on the Judiciary Committee, told the AP he had concerns about how the White House has tried to “air-drop” somebody into the vacancy.
The attorney did not go through the usual process Texas senators use to vet nominees, and Democrats have zeroed in on his limited ties to Texas, which they say amount to just a clerkship in Houston while spending the rest of his career in Ohio or Washington, DC.
Race against the clock
To push through, Grassley has previewed an all-gas-no-breaks approach in his committee – an approach he said Tuesday was justified by signals that Democrats could block any nominee Trump tried to put forward next Congress.
“They’re planning to stonewall a president’s ability to appoint judges – now that is what is unprecedented,” Grassley said at Tuesday’s committee meeting. “So yes, I’m working. I’m going to work hard to get judges confirmed quickly during the lame duck session.”

items.article_content:
An Israeli strike on a hospital in southern Gaza overnight Wednesday killed at least six people, including a doctor and a child, Palestinian officials say.
The strike on Nasser Hospital shortly after midnight hit the complex’s surgery unit, according to a Gaza Civil Defense spokesman. The attack tore through part of the hospital in the dark of night, Ezz Eddine Abu Sabha said, leaving charred debris scattered across the destroyed unit.
The strike killed 52-year-old Dr. Rizk Abu Shaira, Abu Sabha said, as well as a 13-year-old boy who was supposed to have surgery. A total of 40 people were injured in the Israeli strike, including two doctors who are in critical condition.
“They say there is a ceasefire. Where is there a ceasefire? Since the ceasefire, there are more massacres,” said Maryam Abu Hatab, whose brother was killed in the strike. “There are massacres every day in markets, in universities, in the streets. The donkey carts stood by us more than the world’s countries.”
Footage from inside the hospital showed two bombs, one of which failed to explode. A label on the bomb identified it as a US-manufactured GBU-39/B, a 250-pound bomb that has been supplied to Israel.
Munition fragments and an unexploded bomb at Nasser Hospital following an Israeli airstrike.
Abed Rahim Khatib/Anadolu/Getty Images
“I was asleep when suddenly I was covered with dust and glass,” said Atiya Abu Basir, an elderly patient at the hospital. “I couldn’t walk because I just had surgery.”
Despite a nominal US-brokered ceasefire signed more than a year ago, Israel has carried out near-daily strikes in Gaza. According to the United Nations, Israeli forces have killed more than 1,400 people in Gaza since the ceasefire, and there is no fully functioning hospital in the devastated enclave.
In a statement, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said they targeted the commander of Hamas’ Khan Younis Brigade, Muhammad Abu Ismail, as well as “additional terrorists who were hiding inside the Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis.” The IDF said he planned and advanced attacks on Israeli forces and civilians.
CNN reached out to the IDF to ask if Abu Ismail had been killed in the strike and what measures were taken to reduce the risk to civilians.
Board of Peace chides Israel
Displaced Palestinians clear rainwater from flooded tents in Gaza City on November 7.
Ahmad Salem/Bloomberg/Getty Images
Earlier this week, the US-led Board of Peace, which is tasked with overseeing the ceasefire in Gaza, chided Israel for what it called an “insufficient” response to Gaza flooding. Seasonal rains swamped tens of thousands of tents across the coastal enclave, where nearly two million Palestinians are displaced, according to the United Nations.
“The urgent entry and distribution of essential shelter, sanitation, drainage, and other winterization supplies is critical to protecting civilians,” the board said in a statement Monday, calling on Israel to allow more temporary shelters, waste management, and other supplies.
Israel said that more than 91,000 tents had entered Gaza ahead winter, but refused to allow in the heavy equipment needed for large-scale cleanup and rubble removal efforts.
“The reconstruction of Gaza can only begin after Hamas fully disarms,” said Israel’s Coordinator for Government Activities in the Territories.

Twice in recent days, the administration has offered remarkable initial salvos in the looming investigative battles … The post The Trump team’s hypocrisy reaches new levels with warning letter to Democrats appeared first on Egypt Independent .
items.excerpt: After years of Republicans going to extraordinary lengths to politicize congressional oversight and target President Donald Trump’s enemies, his administration is now issuing stark warnings to Democrats to not politicize congressional oversight to target Trump and those around him. Twice in recent days, the administration has offered remarkable initial salvos in the looming investigative battles … The post The Trump team’s hypocrisy reaches new levels with warning letter to Democrats appeared first on Egypt Independent .
items.article_content:
After years of Republicans going to extraordinary lengths to politicize congressional oversight and target President Donald Trump’s enemies, his administration is now issuing stark warnings to Democrats to not politicize congressional oversight to target Trump and those around him.
Twice in recent days, the administration has offered remarkable initial salvos in the looming investigative battles between it and the incoming Democratic-controlled Congress.
During a CNN interview on Sunday, Attorney General Todd Blanche left open the possibility of the Justice Department prosecuting Democratic lawmakers who threaten to investigate Trump administration officials too overzealously.
And on Wednesday, White House counsel Will Scharf issued a letter cautioning the House Oversight Committee against forthcoming investigations and saying the administration “will not be extorted.”
Both are rather rich, considering the recent history of Republicans leveraging governmental power to target Trump’s foes — in ways with little if any modern precedent.
In the Wednesday letter to incoming House Oversight Committee Chair Robert Garcia, Scharf warns that Democrats’ oversight “must further a legitimate legislative task,” rather than trying to serve the criminal-prosecution functions of the executive and judicial branches.
He cites the possibility of “unlawful process motivated by animus, pettiness, hatred, or any other unlawful motive.” He also cites “abusive and capricious threats” from Democratic lawmakers.
(Garcia, a California Democrat, responded by saying the House “will not be deterred by baseless threats from a weaponized DOJ or from the president’s lawyers.”)
Attorney General Todd Blanche speaks during a news conference at the Robert F. Kennedy Department of Justice building on September 30.
Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images
Scharf’s letter echoes Blanche’s comments from Sunday. After Trump posted on social media that Democrats’ investigative threats amounted to “extortion at the highest level,” Blanche left open the possibility that the Democrats could be prosecuted for it.
Blanche cited Garcia’s two-word statement to the administration on election night: “LAWYER UP.”
“If that doesn’t bother you, if that doesn’t bother your viewers, then we really need to kind of wake up in this country, because it certainly bothers me,” Blanche told CNN’s Dana Bash.
The GOP has explicitly told Democrats to ‘lawyer up,’ too
But Trump and his allies have issued plenty of very similar threats to Democrats in recent years:
In 2023, now-FBI Director Kash Patel warned: “We’re going to come after the people in the media who lied about American citizens, who helped Joe Biden rig presidential elections — we’re going to come after you.”
Then-Trump Justice Department official Ed Martin in May 2025 amplified a post that stated, “Lawyer up, Lawfare Democrats.”
GOP Sen. Eric Schmitt of Missouri in October 2025 urged figures mentioned in the “Arctic Frost” investigation to “lawyer up.”
Current GOP House Oversight Committee Chair James Comer in January told Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz to “lawyer up” over fraud that took place on his watch in Minnesota.
Trump has pursued extensive legal retribution
Still, perhaps the bigger point is this: The administration long ago vacated the moral high ground when it comes to “abusive and capricious threats” of investigations “motivated by animus, pettiness, hatred.”
Trump himself has targeted scores of his political foes, often for non-existent or thinly constructed supposed offenses. And he has repeatedly acknowledged he can’t set aside his hatred of his enemies — including in a “60 Minutes” interview that aired this past weekend.
A November 2025 Reuters investigation found that, in less than a year of Trump’s second term, he had targeted at least 470 people, organizations and institutions for retribution.
Tellingly, his administration has investigated people responsible for virtually every major investigation and court case against Trump.
And the president at one point explicitly signaled he was out not for accountability, but for “retribution.”
“For those who have been wronged and betrayed, I am your retribution,” he said in March 2023.
His Justice Department has regularly pursued criminal cases against Trump’s foes based on the thinnest of evidence, often at Trump’s urging.
Several of these cases have fallen apart — either because they didn’t clear the typically very low bar of getting a grand jury to vote to indict, or because those investigating the matter clearly couldn’t produce the goods.
Cassidy Hutchinson, a top former aide to Trump White House chief of staff Mark Meadows, testifies during the sixth hearing by the House Select Committee to Investigate the January 6th Attack on the U.S. Capitol on June 28, 2022 in Washington, DC.
Brandon Bell/Getty Images
That includes:
Failed indictments against six congressional Democrats (for telling military service members and intelligence officials not to follow illegal orders)
Multiple failed indictments against New York Attorney General Letitia James
A failed indictment of January 6 witness Cassidy Hutchinson
Cases against James and former FBI Director James Comey that were thrown out. (Comey was later re-indicted twice in cases that legal experts are skeptical of)
A series of failed efforts to legally target Trump’s foes like California Sen. Adam Schiff and Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook for supposed mortgage issues
A later-abandoned criminal probe of then-Fed Chair Jerome Powell for cost overruns in a Fed renovation
And despite Trump’s allies having accused the Biden administration of political prosecutions against Trump, there is far more evidence that Trump pushed these probes than there is that former President Joe Biden was involved in getting Trump indicted.
The GOP also politicized congressional oversight, based on little evidence
These are criminal investigations, rather than congressional oversight. But even on congressional investigations, it’s pretty difficult for Republicans to claim they haven’t done what the Trump administration is warning Democrats not to do.
Ahead of an expected 2024 matchup between Trump and Biden, the House GOP launched an impeachment inquiry against Biden that regularly involved overstating evidence of suppose corruption in the “Biden crime family.” One of their central attacks on Biden relied on an unverified claim from an FBI informant who later pleaded guilty to fabricating it.
Republicans ultimately couldn’t even get enough of their own GOP members to vote to impeach Biden, despite not needing any Democratic votes. So the inquiry never served any concrete legislative purpose — the line the Trump administration is now trying to draw with Democrats.
In the same Congress, Republicans also launched a special committee supposedly probing the “weaponization” of government by the Biden administration. It, too, vastly overstated evidence of wrongdoing and went out with a whimper.
Polls show Americans differentiate between the parties’ approaches
Still, the hard-edged front from the Trump administration in recent days at least makes some political sense. Theoretically, the administration could muddy the waters by arguing that Democrats are being overzealous in their intent to scrutinize the administration.
But the polls have suggested that Americans see the difference between how Democrats and Republicans have handled these issues.
While majorities of Americans saw Trump’s indictments as legitimate, polling last year showed Americans said by double digits that the cases against Trump’s foes were politicized and illegitimate.
Americans also took a rather dim view of the Biden impeachment inquiry. And an early 2023 poll showed Americans said by 20 points that the GOP’s “weaponization” committee was mostly “just an attempt to score political points.”
Fast forward to today, and Americans see plenty that’s worthwhile for the Democratic-controlled Congress to investigate.

items.article_content:
New York —
Nvidia, Jensen Huang, an alleged subordinate and a suspected Chinese spy are at the center of a soap opera captivating Wall Street, Silicon Valley and Washington.
And, like every other soap opera, this one appears to involve at least a dose of deception. Did Nvidia’s rockstar CEO mislead his bosses on the board of directors? Did Nvidia and its board conceal from investors what was really going on?
Unlike a typical daytime drama, the stakes here are epic. Untangling who lied to whom could determine the fate of trillions of dollars.
Huang is viewed as so critical to Nvidia’s success that the chipmaker could lose $1 trillion of market value if the CEO is pushed out, according to estimates from Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co.
“Jensen has created a black eye moment for himself and Nvidia and now has created a spider web of complexity that Wall Street, Silicon Valley, DC and the global tech ecosystem are trying to figure out what is next,” Ives wrote in a report to clients on Wednesday night.
Suspected Chinese spy
Jensen Huang and Alice Huang are seen walking around an exclusive golf resort in San Martin, California. CNN geolocated the still to the luxury CordeValle resort.
From Social Media
Huang’s enormous value to Nvidia and the AI industry is exactly why Huang would be an obvious high-value target for foreign intelligence as the world engages in an AI arms race.
And that’s where the first, and most obvious deception appears to come from.
Intelligence agencies are known to lure their targets through deceptive schemes like the honey trap suspected in this case.
Jensen Huang has admitted to an extramarital affair, and US officials have told CNN that he had a relationship with Alice Huang, who they have concluded is a Chinese spy.
Nvidia’s board is investigating whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
US intelligence concluded in a classified memo issued in May that Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Nvidia customer Megaspeed, was a Chinese intelligence asset, according to CNN reporting.
Crucially, Megaspeed was under federal investigation for allegedly diverting highly coveted US semiconductors to entities in China in violation of US export controls.
Did Jensen Huang mislead the board?
But that may not be where the deception stopped.
Gary Gensler, former chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission, said that Nvidia’s board investigation must determine if their rockstar CEO was honest with them.
“If he misled the board, it’s likely they remove him from the job even though they don’t have a groomed successor,” Gensler, now a professor at MIT, told CNN Wednesday night.
Misleading the board is no small matter, especially in this case. Failing to disclose an active romantic relationship with a major customer could be viewed as concealing a glaring conflict of interest.
That’s something that could be determined by the independent investigation Nvidia’s board has launched.
If that investigation concludes that Huang deliberately misled his bosses on the board about a massive conflict of interest, the board would have clear grounds to fire him, according to Charles Whitehead, professor of business law at Cornell Law School. And failing to do so could open directors to their own legal exposure.
The alleged second affair
Nvidia shares plummeted Wednesday night after The New York Times reported that Huang had an extramarital affair with an employee who reports to him.
Gensler said these allegations raise the question of whether Huang misled the board about this matter, too.
He said board members investigating CEOs typically ask them a “standard” question at the start: “Is there anything else you need to tell us?”
“Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me,” Gensler said.
The imploding corporate defense
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang signs a magazine cover for his fans in Taipei, Taiwan January 17, 2025.
Ann Wang/Reuters
Another key question is whether Nvidia and Huang were upfront with the public and investors as journalists were digging into this story.
“Did he participate with his staff in misleading public investors?” Gensler asked.
The former SEC chair noted that Nvidia provided an explanation on this controversy that has aged particularly poorly – even though it was delivered barely two weeks ago.
“Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected,” an Nvidia spokesman told The New York Times. “Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year.”
That statement appears to be directly contradicted by the fact that Huang has since admitted to an affair and the board has launched an investigation.
‘You just can’t lie about it’
Of course, it’s now clear that this relationship was anything but routine.
Even though an extramarital affair could be looked at as a personal issue, making a false statement to the public would open up Nvidia to allegations of making a material corporate misstatement.
It would be hard to argue this matter is not material. Nvidia’s share price plummeted by as much as 9% intraday on Monday after Huang admitted an affair and the board launched an investigation.
“The movement in the stock price tells us that this was material information. So that passes one test of law. And the second test is: Did you mislead the public about material information? And it appears that way,” Gensler said.
A shareholder lawsuit, filed Monday in a California court, alleges Nvidia and Jensen Huang deceived investors in their responses to media reports about the affair.
“You can have as many affairs with Chinese spies as you want under federal law, you just can’t lie about it,” said Ann Lipton, professor at Colorado Law School at the University of Colorado, Boulder.
What did the board know and when did it know it?
Another question is whether Nvidia’s board of directors misled investors about this matter.
Federal agents briefed lawmakers roughly a year ago that they suspected Huang was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.”
What’s less clear is how much the company knew about these suspicions.
But if Nvidia’s board did know, shareholders could argue the board deceived investors by failing to disclose it.
Another major question is whether Nvidia and its CEO knew – or should have known – that Megaspeed was allegedly smuggling cutting-edge AI chips to China in violation of export controls.
“This could, depending on what was said in the bedroom, escalate to a 10b-5 claim (an SEC rule that prohibits securities fraud, material misstatements and deceptive schemes) and potentially even criminal liability to the extent he knowingly aided a violation of the trade restrictions,” said Whitehead.
Nvidia said on Sunday the board has “no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised.”
‘Very awkward’ spot for the board
This matter is further complicated by how critical Huang is viewed to Nvidia’s success – and the fact he has no heir apparent.
“From the board’s point of view, they have a very tough choice in front of them. They have a founder who is at the heart of this company, no groomed successor,” Gensler said. “What do they do if they find out that he misled the board? What do they do if they find out that he was aware that some information may have been shared with the Chinese inappropriately.”
Nvidia’s board announced on Tuesday it has hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, a prestigious Wall Street law firm, to “conduct a thorough and independent investigation.”
Asked about his experience with boards hiring law firms to conduct so-called independent investigations, Gensler said it’s not clear how fair and balanced this report will ultimately be.
“Oftentimes, boards of directors would like the lawyers to do a report that doesn’t escalate the problem but helps resolve the crisis at the moment,” Gensler said.

items.excerpt: Angola’s ambassador to Egypt, Maquento Sebastião Lopes, credited Presidents João Lourenço and Abdel Fattah al-Sisi with giving a significant boost to relations between the two countries in recent years, at a reception in Cairo on Wednesday marking the 51st anniversary of Angola’s independence and 50 years of diplomatic ties with Egypt. items.article_content:
Angola’s ambassador to Egypt, Maquento Sebastião Lopes, credited Presidents João Lourenço and Abdel Fattah al-Sisi with giving a significant boost to relations between the two countries in recent years, at a reception in Cairo on Wednesday marking the 51st anniversary of Angola’s independence and 50 years of diplomatic ties with Egypt.
Through regular contact and dialogue at the highest level, the two leaders had strengthened political trust and identified new areas of mutually beneficial co-operation, Lopes said, citing their shared views on Africa’s development, peace and stability on the continent and African economic integration. He pointed to the institutionalisation of the Angola-Egypt Bilateral Commission as concrete evidence of a shared will to turn strong political relations into tangible benefits for both peoples.
The two countries established diplomatic relations in February 1976, three months after Angola’s independence from Portugal on 11 November 1975. Lopes said their friendship predated formal ties, recalling Egypt’s support, grounded in pan-Africanism and self-determination, for national liberation movements across Africa.
In the 51 years since independence, Angola had achieved and consolidated peace, strengthened its institutions, rebuilt the country and expanded access to education and health care, while playing an increasingly important role in promoting stability and security in Africa, he said.
With Africa accelerating economic integration, Lopes said Angola and Egypt were well placed to build strategic partnerships in agriculture, industry, infrastructure, transport, energy, water and mineral resources, technological innovation and training. “The complementarity of our economies and the quality of our political relations offer solid foundations for an even more promising future,” he said.
A day of commemoration
The celebrations were held under the slogan “United for a Democratic, One and Indivisible Angola”, which the ambassador said expressed Angolans’ commitment to national unity, democracy, the rule of law and the defence of the country’s sovereignty. He paid tribute to the founders of the Angolan nation and to the statesmen, diplomats, academics, business people and citizens of both countries who had built the relationship.
The reception, held at a Cairo hotel, was attended by members of the Egyptian government, the diplomatic corps, academics, students, business people and members of the Angolan community in Egypt. The embassy screened a 10-minute documentary, “Angola and Egypt: 50 Years Building the Future”, on the history of relations between the two countries.
Earlier in the day, Lopes and other Angolan diplomats laid a wreath at the monument to António Agostinho Neto, Angola’s first president, in Heroes’ Park in Zamalek. The bust was unveiled in September as part of the 50th anniversary celebrations.
Egypt eyes investment
Speaking on behalf of Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty, Ambassador Khaled Aref, Egypt’s deputy assistant foreign minister for Southern Africa, congratulated President João Lourenço, his government and the Angolan people, saying that since 1975 Angola had written “a remarkable story of resilience, unity and progress”.
Aref said Egypt was encouraging its companies to invest in Angola in infrastructure, housing, urban development and agriculture, and hoped Egyptian oil and gas companies would enter the Angolan market. Egypt had long experience in building gas networks and would be glad to share it with Angola, the official said.
The speech highlighted a busy period in relations. In early October, Lourenço co-chaired with President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi the summit of the founding states of the African Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD) at the Alamein Africa Forum, and took part in the African Union’s mid-year co-ordination meeting in New Alamein.
A shared history
Aref also referred to the Agostinho Neto monument, describing it as having a lasting place in the heart of the Egyptian capital. The two countries signed a cultural co-operation agreement in Cairo in September.
The official recalled the two peoples’ shared love of football and the Angolan players who have won over Egyptian fans, and said the friendship between Egypt and Angola went beyond diplomacy and economic partnership.
The official closed with a toast to Egyptian-Angolan friendship and to African unity.

items.article_content:
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi has issued a decree allocating about 26,690 feddans of state-owned land in the Red Sea governorate to the finance ministry to reduce public debt and issue sovereign sukuk, as Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly reviewed progress towards the government’s debt targets.
The decree, published in the Official Gazette, amends Article 1 of Presidential Decree No. 222 of 2026. The original text allocated the same plot, about 112.1mn sq m of land owned privately by the state, for issuing sovereign sukuk only. The amendment adds public debt reduction to its permitted uses.
Debt-reduction meeting
Madbouly met Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk at the government’s headquarters in the New Administrative Capital to follow up on the recommendations of the Egypt Forum 2026 on reducing the debt of budget-sector bodies, in co-operation with state economic authorities. Also attending were May Adel, assistant finance minister for public debt management, and Mahmoud Hodhod, head of the ministry’s bank financing and investment unit.
The prime minister called debt reduction a top government priority, aimed at easing the cost of servicing it and freeing resources for priority sectors and public services. The forum’s recommendations set a path to bring public debt down to about 69.5% of GDP by 2030, with fixed ceilings on public debt, external debt and sovereign guarantees.
Kouchouk said the ratio of budget-sector debt to GDP had been falling since the 2023/24 fiscal year and had dropped by about 14 percentage points between June 2023 and June 2026. External debt of budget-sector bodies was cut by the equivalent of about 3.9% of GDP in 2025/26, he said.
The finance minister presented proposals to speed up debt reduction, achieve higher growth and diversify funding through new and innovative instruments. Madbouly directed officials to draw up a detailed plan setting out specific tasks for each ministry and government body, to be presented to the president.

The two-day summit, held on 11 and 12 […]
items.excerpt: Egypt’s Minister of Local Development and Environment Manal Awad represented President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi at the leaders’ summit of the COP31 UN climate conference in the Turkish city of Antalya on Wednesday, calling for affordable climate finance for developing countries and a shift from pledges to delivery. items.article_content:
Egypt’s Minister of Local Development and Environment Manal Awad represented President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi at the leaders’ summit of the COP31 UN climate conference in the Turkish city of Antalya on Wednesday, calling for affordable climate finance for developing countries and a shift from pledges to delivery.
The two-day summit, held on 11 and 12 November under the theme “Towards a Sustainable, Resilient and Equitable Future”, was opened by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and attended by UN Secretary-General António Guterres. Egypt’s environment ministry said representatives of 95 countries took part.
Egypt’s priorities
Awad said Egypt wanted the conference to move to real implementation in four areas: expanding clean electricity, moving away from fossil fuels, providing affordable climate finance for developing countries, and strengthening resilience to global warming.
She said financial and technical support for developing countries topped the agenda, amid growing calls to speed up funding for adaptation, for loss and damage, and for the transition to a low-carbon economy. The opening sessions focused on the links between climate change and food security, agriculture and public health, including more efficient water use and more resilient food systems, she said.
Egypt is presenting its vision for “just climate action” at the summit, Awad said. She is also taking part in a session of African environment ministers and the D-8 group of developing countries, and holding bilateral meetings to promote green investment.
An unusual presidency
COP31 runs from 9 to 20 November at the Antalya Expo Centre. It is the first UN climate conference to be led under a shared arrangement agreed at COP30 in Belém, Brazil, last year, which ended a long standoff between Turkey and Australia, both of which had bid to host the 2026 talks.
Under the deal, Turkey hosts the conference and holds the presidency through its environment minister Murat Kurum, while Australia’s climate and energy minister Chris Bowen serves as “President of Negotiations”, with authority to run the formal talks in consultation with Turkey. A pre-COP meeting was held in Fiji in October to give Pacific states a greater voice.
Kurum has said he wants Antalya to focus on turning existing climate commitments into action rather than setting new targets, and the presidency is drafting an Antalya Declaration for leaders to endorse. Holding the leaders’ summit on the third and fourth days of the conference, rather than at the start, is meant to give political momentum to the negotiators. Leaders who did not speak this week will deliver their national statements on 17 and 18 November.
Egypt hosted COP27 in Sharm El-Sheikh in 2022, where countries agreed to set up a fund for loss and damage suffered by vulnerable nations.

items.article_content:
Egypt’s Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty met Liu Xianfa, the Chinese government’s special envoy for African affairs, in Cairo on Wednesday to discuss joint co-operation between the two countries in Africa and developments across the region.
Abdelatty welcomed Liu on his first visit to Cairo and praised the comprehensive strategic partnership between Egypt and China, according to foreign ministry spokesman Ambassador Nader Zaki. He said Egypt wanted to expand trilateral co-operation with China to carry out development projects in key sectors across Africa, and to support capacity building and training for African officials through the ministry’s agencies.
These include the Cairo International Center for Conflict Resolution, Peacekeeping and Peacebuilding, which is organising the sixth edition of the Aswan Forum for Sustainable Peace and Development later this month.
Liu conveyed China’s appreciation for Egypt’s civilisation and history, and said he was impressed by the modernisation of the country’s infrastructure, particularly the New Administrative Capital.
Regional security and the Nile
The two discussed the situation in the Horn of Africa, the Red Sea, Sudan and Somalia. Abdelatty stressed the importance of supporting national state institutions and preserving the unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity of the region’s countries, and called for the security of the Red Sea and freedom of navigation to be protected.
He also restated Egypt’s position on its water security, calling for adherence to international law and rejecting unilateral measures on the Nile.
The two sides agreed to keep co-ordinating in international forums on regional issues of shared concern.

items.title: Egypt’s Investment, Planning ministers discuss stronger economic ties with US
items.summary: Mohamed Farid, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade, and Ahmed Rostom, Minister of Planning and Economic Development, held talks with US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to explore ways to deepen trade and investment relations and discuss key developments in US trade policy and their implications for bilateral trade, in a manner that serves the shared […]
items.excerpt: Mohamed Farid, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade, and Ahmed Rostom, Minister of Planning and Economic Development, held talks with US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to explore ways to deepen trade and investment relations and discuss key developments in US trade policy and their implications for bilateral trade, in a manner that serves the shared […]
items.article_content:
Mohamed Farid, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade, and Ahmed Rostom, Minister of Planning and Economic Development, held talks with US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to explore ways to deepen trade and investment relations and discuss key developments in US trade policy and their implications for bilateral trade, in a manner that serves the shared economic interests of both countries.
The meeting took place on the sidelines of the Egyptian ministers’ participation in the B20 Business Summit 2026 in Washington, DC, as part of the preparatory activities for the G20 meetings.
During the meeting, Farid reviewed several issues related to strengthening cooperation in trade remedies and exchanging expertise in this area in accordance with fair technical and commercial standards. He said both sides had agreed to continue technical consultations between the relevant authorities to support the fair competitiveness of Egyptian exports and facilitate bilateral trade.
Farid noted that the Ministry is working to launch the National Foreign Direct Investment Strategy, which aims to identify priority sectors and direct investment promotion efforts towards investments with high added value.
He pointed out that advanced technology sectors, including information and communications technology (ICT), automotive and smart mobility technologies, and cybersecurity, offer promising opportunities for cooperation with US companies in manufacturing, technology transfer and related services.
He also highlighted ongoing efforts to strengthen coordination and integration among various entities and institutions in preparation for launching the Economic Entities Platform, which aims to streamline the investor experience by covering all requirements, from business establishment through to operation.
For his part, Rostom reviewed the Egyptian state’s plan to address the repercussions of regional geopolitical developments, stressing that the economy had demonstrated resilience thanks to proactive fiscal and monetary policy measures.
He noted that the economy recorded real growth of 5.1% in FY2025/2026, compared with approximately 4.4% in the previous fiscal year.
Rostom also highlighted progress in reducing inflation, noting that the headline inflation rate declined to 12% in October 2026, from 12.8% in September, while core inflation fell to 14.1%.

items.title: Egypt’s FM discusses regional tensions with Kuwait, development cooperation with France
items.summary: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty discussed efforts to de-escalate regional tensions and strengthen economic ties with his Kuwaiti counterpart on Wednesday, while also holding talks in Paris with the head of the French Development Agency (AFD) on development projects in transport, energy, healthcare and infrastructure. In a phone call with Kuwaiti Foreign Minister Jarrah Jaber […]
items.excerpt: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty discussed efforts to de-escalate regional tensions and strengthen economic ties with his Kuwaiti counterpart on Wednesday, while also holding talks in Paris with the head of the French Development Agency (AFD) on development projects in transport, energy, healthcare and infrastructure. In a phone call with Kuwaiti Foreign Minister Jarrah Jaber […]
items.article_content:
Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty discussed efforts to de-escalate regional tensions and strengthen economic ties with his Kuwaiti counterpart on Wednesday, while also holding talks in Paris with the head of the French Development Agency (AFD) on development projects in transport, energy, healthcare and infrastructure.
In a phone call with Kuwaiti Foreign Minister Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, the two ministers discussed preparations for the next meeting of the Egyptian-Kuwaiti Joint Committee, which is scheduled to be held in Kuwait with the participation of ministries and government agencies from both countries.
Abdelatty stressed Egypt’s keenness for the committee’s meeting to deliver tangible cooperation projects, particularly in investment and trade, while promoting reciprocal investments and expanding cooperation in priority sectors.
The ministers also exchanged views on regional developments. Abdelatty called for continued coordination between Cairo and Kuwait to contain escalating tensions and prevent the region from sliding into another military confrontation.
He reaffirmed Egypt’s support for political and diplomatic solutions, stressing that dialogue remains the primary means of addressing regional crises.
Separately, Abdelatty met with French Development Agency Director-General Christophe Lecourtier in Paris on Tuesday, on the sidelines of a Group of Seven (G7) ministerial meeting with partner countries.
The meeting reviewed Egypt’s economic and development cooperation with AFD, including projects that had advanced during 2026 in transport, energy, green industry, healthcare, housing and infrastructure.
Abdelatty said Egypt’s partnership with the agency, which spans nearly two decades, had supported development projects aimed at improving public services and promoting economic and social development.
He also highlighted the pressures facing Egypt’s economy as a result of regional and global developments, reaffirming the government’s commitment to implementing its economic reform programme and structural reforms. He added that Egypt was working to strengthen its position as a regional hub for transport and logistics.
Lecourtier reaffirmed AFD’s commitment to supporting Egypt’s development priorities and expressed interest in visiting the country to review projects financed by the agency.
The Foreign Ministry statements did not disclose details of any new financing or the value of the projects discussed with AFD. They also did not specify a date for the next Egyptian-Kuwaiti Joint Committee meeting or identify any agreements expected to be signed.

items.title: Ahmed Fathy: ‘Za’ar’ blends horror and comedy as I seek roles that add something new to my career
items.summary: Some actors simply appear on screen, while others leave a lasting impression on audiences, building a distinctive presence through a variety of productions until they become an integral part of the artistic landscape and viewers’ emotional world. Whether through comedy, which brings joy to audiences, or tragedy, which explores the depth of human emotions, an […]
items.excerpt: Some actors simply appear on screen, while others leave a lasting impression on audiences, building a distinctive presence through a variety of productions until they become an integral part of the artistic landscape and viewers’ emotional world. Whether through comedy, which brings joy to audiences, or tragedy, which explores the depth of human emotions, an […]
items.article_content:
Some actors simply appear on screen, while others leave a lasting impression on audiences, building a distinctive presence through a variety of productions until they become an integral part of the artistic landscape and viewers’ emotional world. Whether through comedy, which brings joy to audiences, or tragedy, which explores the depth of human emotions, an actor’s ability to diversify and reinvent himself remains one of the most important hallmarks of genuine talent.
Actor Ahmed Fathy is among the artists who have established a recognisable presence in comedy while also exploring different experiences that demonstrate his versatility and range as a performer. He continues to seek out new characters and challenges, refusing to confine himself to a single artistic genre.
Throughout his career, Fathy has appeared in a diverse range of film and television productions, sharing the screen with some of Egypt’s most prominent artists, foremost among them the legendary Adel Imam. He speaks of their collaboration with profound admiration, describing it as an exceptional experience that had a lasting impact on his professional journey. He also reflects on the influence of the late Nour El-Sherif, whom he regards as an outstanding artistic and humanitarian role model.
In this interview with Daily News Egypt, Fathy discusses the differences between comedy and tragedy, his experience working alongside Adel Imam, the place Nour El-Sherif holds in his heart, and his assessment of Mohamed Saad’s artistic career. He also talks about his upcoming projects and recent productions, including the film ‘Za’ar’, his experience in ‘Moallef Wa Mokhreg Wa Harami’, and his participation in the fifth season of the television series ‘El Leaba’. In addition, he discusses the importance of new cinematic initiatives seeking to bring cinema closer to audiences and shares his vision for the future of comedy in Egyptian cinema.
Ahmed Fathy
How do you view the difference between comedy and tragedy in acting?
A true actor should never confine himself exclusively to comedy or tragedy. He must possess the acting skills that enable him to move seamlessly between comic situations and different human and dramatic emotions. Talent cannot be restricted to a single genre; it requires the ability to portray diverse characters and convey both humorous situations and profound emotions.
You have appeared in numerous comedy productions, but you have also explored dramatic roles. Which of those experiences stand out most to you?
I have taken part in several dramatic productions. Although they have not been numerous, some have left a lasting impression on audiences. One notable example is the television series ‘Halet Eshq’, through which I was able to reveal a different side of my acting abilities.
You have spoken with great admiration about the legendary Adel Imam. How would you describe your experience working with him and the influence he had on you?
Adel Imam is a truly remarkable man, both personally and professionally, and possesses extraordinary charisma. I have never met anyone with such a remarkable presence and influence. He treats the script with tremendous respect, almost considering it sacred. He examines every written word carefully and does not accept the addition of even a single word that is not already included in the screenplay.
I worked with him on two television series, and my professional experience before collaborating with him was completely different from what it became afterwards. His extraordinary stardom did not happen by chance; it is the result of many years of hard work, dedication and study. Standing alongside him is like receiving a certificate of birth as an actor in the world of stardom. He is an artistic legend who will never be repeated.
Which film do you consider one of Adel Imam’s most significant works?
I would choose ‘El-Hareef’, directed by Mohamed Khan. I consider it one of his most important films and a landmark in the history of Egyptian cinema. It remains a shining achievement because of its artistic value and distinctive cinematic identity.
You have also spoken about the influence of the late actor Nour El-Sherif. How did he affect you?
Nour El-Sherif is one of the people who influenced me most on a human level. He had his own distinctive school of acting and represented an exceptional artistic and humanitarian model. His legacy has left a profound impact on the generations that followed him.
Many people have praised Mohamed Saad’s comic performances. What is your opinion of him?
Mohamed Saad is one of the most prominent artists to have contributed to comedy. He has an exceptional ability to create characters and portray them in a distinctive way, which has given him a unique identity within this genre.
After years of working in the entertainment industry, how would you describe your relationship with audiences, and what gives an actor a lasting place in people’s hearts?
The audience is the true judge of an actor, and it is the audience that grants him continuity and stardom. Success is not achieved simply by appearing in a production or gaining visibility on screen. It comes from the ability to connect with people emotionally and leave a lasting impression on them.
An actor must always remain connected to audiences and offer productions that carry genuine value while providing viewers with real enjoyment. I believe diversity in roles and continuous reinvention are among the most important factors that help an artist maintain a lasting relationship with the public.
You were recently honoured in recognition of your artistic career and your participation in the ‘Cinema Café’ platform during the third edition of the Very Short Film Festival in Suez. How did you receive this honour, and what does it mean to you?
The honour was presented by the festival’s management, headed by Osama Abounar, with journalist and writer Kadry El-Haggar serving as festival director. The recognition acknowledged my artistic journey and my participation in the platform’s activities.
I am grateful for this gesture, particularly because it comes within the framework of a festival dedicated to very short films and committed to presenting new experiences that bring cinema closer to audiences.
Could you tell us more about the ‘Cinema Café’ programme and its role in the festival?
The session was held as part of the ‘Cinema Café’ platform for very short films, alongside the activities of the festival’s third edition. The concept revolves around screening films in cafés rather than conventional cinema halls, with artists and audiences attending together, followed by open discussions about the films.
This concept brings back something of the atmosphere of cinema’s early beginnings and creates direct interaction between filmmakers and viewers.
The discussion was moderated by Kadry El-Haggar and focused on my artistic experiences and my perspective on acting.
Ahmed Fathy
How important are initiatives like these in supporting short films and engaging audiences?
Such programmes make cinema more accessible to people and create opportunities for direct interaction. The festival is keen to bring audiences and filmmakers together in a social setting, enriching the artistic experience and encouraging discussions about the content and ideas presented in films.
How do you see the future of comedy in Egyptian cinema? Has producing a successful comedy film become more challenging as audience tastes continue to evolve?
Comedy is one of the most challenging forms of acting because it requires a strong sense of timing and the ability to portray a character naturally and convincingly. Audiences now have a wide range of choices, which means artists must offer fresh ideas and different characters rather than simply repeat previous experiences.
I believe genuine comedy emerges from the character and the situation itself. It should make audiences laugh naturally, without relying on forced or artificial humour

items.title: Nine Japanese firms explore investment opportunities in Egypt’s green energy sector
items.summary: The Egyptian Commercial Service (ECS) at the Egyptian Embassy in Tokyo organised a high-level roundtable to explore opportunities for Japanese investment in Egypt’s green energy sector, with a focus on renewable energy and green hydrogen. The event, titled “Promoting Investment and Improving the Investment Climate across Egypt’s Green Energy Value Chain,” was chaired by Plenipotentiary […]
items.excerpt: The Egyptian Commercial Service (ECS) at the Egyptian Embassy in Tokyo organised a high-level roundtable to explore opportunities for Japanese investment in Egypt’s green energy sector, with a focus on renewable energy and green hydrogen. The event, titled “Promoting Investment and Improving the Investment Climate across Egypt’s Green Energy Value Chain,” was chaired by Plenipotentiary […]
items.article_content:
The Egyptian Commercial Service (ECS) at the Egyptian Embassy in Tokyo organised a high-level roundtable to explore opportunities for Japanese investment in Egypt’s green energy sector, with a focus on renewable energy and green hydrogen.
The event, titled “Promoting Investment and Improving the Investment Climate across Egypt’s Green Energy Value Chain,” was chaired by Plenipotentiary Minister Commercial Mohamed Abdul Gawad and held in cooperation with the Egyptian Embassy in Tokyo and the Japan Cooperation Center for the Middle East (JCCME), in coordination with Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI).
Egyptian Ambassador to Japan Ragui ElEtreby opened the roundtable, which brought together senior representatives of nine major Japanese corporations operating in the trading, engineering, chemical, and energy sectors.
The meeting also featured representatives of the Institute of Energy Economics, Japan (IEEJ), alongside official delegates from the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE), the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), the Egyptian Exchange (EGX), and Fertiglobe.
Discussions focused on concrete investment opportunities across renewable energy, green hydrogen and its derivatives, feeder industries, and green maritime bunkering.
Participants reviewed investment incentives, financial instruments, risk management strategies, and available operational sites in Ain Sokhna and East Port Said. They also highlighted Egypt’s industrial and logistical advantages as a regional production and export hub, as well as Japan’s support mechanisms for low-carbon hydrogen projects.
Abdel Aziz Al-Sherif, First Undersecretary of the Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade and Head of the Egyptian Commercial Representation, said the roundtable forms part of targeted outreach efforts to align international corporate interests with Egypt’s national priorities.
He stressed the strategic importance of strengthening partnerships with Japan in technology transfer, energy, and project financing, noting that discussions with Japanese companies had already progressed to examining the technical, financial, and operational frameworks for specific ventures.
Coordination will continue among the Egyptian Embassy, JCCME, and relevant Egyptian authorities to arrange follow-up bilateral meetings with participating companies and translate the discussions and investment interest into concrete projects.

items.title: Egypt seeks to mobilise more US investment, capital through DFC partnership
items.summary: Minister of Planning and Economic Development Ahmed Rostom held a meeting with the Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), attended by Egypt’s Ambassador to the United States, Mohamed El-Molla, on the sidelines of the B20 Summit 2026 in Washington, DC. The meeting explored ways to expand bilateral cooperation and […]
items.excerpt: Minister of Planning and Economic Development Ahmed Rostom held a meeting with the Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), attended by Egypt’s Ambassador to the United States, Mohamed El-Molla, on the sidelines of the B20 Summit 2026 in Washington, DC. The meeting explored ways to expand bilateral cooperation and […]
items.article_content:
Minister of Planning and Economic Development Ahmed Rostom held a meeting with the Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), attended by Egypt’s Ambassador to the United States, Mohamed El-Molla, on the sidelines of the B20 Summit 2026 in Washington, DC.
The meeting explored ways to expand bilateral cooperation and mobilise additional US investment and capital for promising sectors and emerging markets, in support of Egypt’s development efforts.
At the beginning of the meeting, Rostom praised the DFC’s pivotal role in promoting private sector investment across the Middle East and North Africa.
Regarding the bilateral partnership, the Planning Minister reaffirmed Egypt’s commitment to deepening economic and trade cooperation with the United States.
He identified digital transformation as a promising pillar of this partnership, particularly in outsourcing, data centres and information technology services.
Rostom also discussed innovative financing mechanisms, reviewing the infrastructure project financing guarantee mechanism developed in partnership with the World Bank to modernise the financing system, strengthen financial stability and ease the burden on the state budget.
The minister formally invited the DFC to explore opportunities to join the mechanism and participate in the portfolio of projects included in its first phase, with the aim of encouraging greater private sector participation.
For her part, the DFC’s Deputy Chief Executive Officer expressed the corporation’s interest in participating in the mechanism, as well as its willingness to invest in the fund of funds that the Ministry of Planning is preparing to launch to finance start-ups and entrepreneurs.
Rostom concluded the discussions by reaffirming the Egyptian government’s commitment to intensifying cooperation with the DFC to strengthen integration between the public and private sectors.
He emphasised the importance of mobilising catalytic financing for priority development areas, particularly the digital economy, energy, logistics and innovative finance.
